attrs.title: Bounding the weights of a mixed sheaf

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be locally of finite type over $\Fq$, put
$X=X_0\times_{\Fq}\Fbar$, and let $K$ be a constructible Weil
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $X$, where $\ell\nmid q$.
Fix an embedding
$\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$ and a real
number $w$. If $K$ is mixed of weights at most $w$, then it is
punctually of weights $\le w$: at every closed point $x$ of $X_0$,
each eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $\operatorname{Frob}_x$ on $K_{\bar x}$
satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|\le q_x^{w/2}$.

If moreover $X_0$ is separated of finite type, $K$ is mixed of
weights at most some real number $u$, and $K$ is punctually of
weights $\le w$, then $K$ is mixed of weights at most $w$.
Thus, for a mixed sheaf in the setting of this chapter, the two
upper bounds are equivalent.

Let $X$ be Noetherian and let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$ be
derived complete with $K_1\in\Dbc(X,\mathbf F_E)$. Choose $[a,b]$
containing the cohomology of $K_1$. Then every $K_n$ lies in
$\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)$ and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, and
$K$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. If the cohomology sheaves of $K_1$
are locally constant on a stratum, then so are those of every $K_n$.
Every $K_n$ lies in $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)$.
Every $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$.
The cohomology of $K$ is concentrated in $[a,b]$.

Rp_{i*}A_{\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}_{p_i}}A_{\mathbf P^1_S}
\tag{6.6}

is the identity.

attrs.title: The class of the diagonal of $\mathbf P^1_S$

objects.body:
Let $S$ be of finite type over $k$ and let $\Lambda$ be a finite
commutative $\ell$-primary ring; we work on the étale sites, and $p_i$ and
$\operatorname{Tr}_{p_i}$ are as above. The diagonal $\Delta$ is a relative
effective Cartier divisor in $\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ over $S$,
and it remains one after every base change $S'\to S$. Let

$$
\delta:\Delta_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}\longrightarrow
\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]
$$

be its cycle class (Lemma [lemma-cycle-class-cartier-divisor]). Then for
$i=1,2$ the composite

$$
s_i:\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}=Rp_{i*}\Delta_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}
\xrightarrow{Rp_{i*}\delta}
Rp_{i*}\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}_{p_i}}\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}
\tag{6.6}
$$

is the identity.

Let $T$ be a $k$-scheme and let $\mathcal L$ be invertible on $C_T$. Then
$Rf_{T,*}\mathcal L$ is locally represented

in the derived category of $\mathcal O_{T'}$-modules. The locus where this complex is an

invertible, its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, and

objects.body:
Let $C$ be a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field and let
$F$ be a constructible sheaf on $C$ with coefficients in $E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.
Then $H^i_c(C,F)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$.

Let $C$ be a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field and let
$F$ be a constructible sheaf on $C$ with coefficients in $E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.
Then $H^i_c(C,F)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$.

For a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on a site, its cohomology and its higher
direct images along a morphism of sites agree with those of its underlying
abelian sheaf. The same holds for $Ru_*$ of bounded below complexes.

Results for abelian sheaves apply to sheaves of modules, because the
cohomology of a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules agrees with the cohomology
of its underlying abelian sheaf [Stacks, [03FD](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03FD)]. Indeed, an
injective sheaf of modules is acyclic for the section functor on
every object of the site, although it need not be injective as an
abelian sheaf. Applying this to the étale objects over the target
gives the same compatibility for $R^qu_*$. Bounded below resolutions
then give it for $Ru_*$.

For a smooth separated curve $C$ of finite type over an algebraically
closed field, one has

$$
H^1(C,\nu_C^*\mathbf G_m)=\operatorname{Pic}(C),
\qquad
H^q(C,\nu_C^*\mathbf G_m)=0\quad(q\geq2).
$$

The identifications are natural under restriction and extension of
the algebraically closed ground field. In particular
$\operatorname{Br}(C)=H^2(C_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_m)=0$.

There is the canonical identification

$$
H^1(C_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\nu_C^*\mathbf G_m)=\operatorname{Pic}(C).
$$
For every $q\geq2$, one has $H^q(C_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\nu_C^*\mathbf G_m)=0$.

For a scheme $Y$, descent for invertible modules identifies
$H^1(Y_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_m)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(Y)$, sending an invertible
sheaf $\mathcal L$ to the class of the $\mathbf G_m$-torsor
$\operatorname{Isom}(\mathcal O_Y,\mathcal L)$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be an étale
monomorphism of schemes. Under these identifications, restriction of
cohomology classes agrees with pullback of line bundles:

$$
f^*[\operatorname{Isom}(\mathcal O_Y,\mathcal L)]
=[\operatorname{Isom}(\mathcal O_X,f^*\mathcal L)]
\quad\text{in }H^1(X_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_m).
$$

For an open immersion $U\hookrightarrow C$, together with the comparison of
[theorem-bounded-below-cohomology-comparison] on $C$ and on $U$, this shows that
the identification of [lemma-cohomology-multiplicative-group--1] is natural under restriction.

Let $g:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes. Under the identifications
$H^1(X_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_m)=\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ and
$H^1(Y_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_m)=\operatorname{Pic}(Y)$ of
[lemma-cohomology-multiplicative-group--3], the pullback map on étale
$\mathbf G_m$-cohomology agrees with pullback of line bundles:

$$
g^*[\operatorname{Isom}(\mathcal O_Y,\mathcal L)]
=[\operatorname{Isom}(\mathcal O_X,g^*\mathcal L)]
\quad\text{in }H^1(X_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_m).
$$

Taking $g:C_{k'}\to C$ for an extension $k'/k$ of algebraically closed
ground fields, together with the comparison of
[theorem-bounded-below-cohomology-comparison] on $C$ and on $C_{k'}$, this shows that
the identification of [lemma-cohomology-multiplicative-group--1] is natural under
extension of the ground field.
One has $\operatorname{Br}(C)=H^2(C_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_m)$.

For a smooth separated scheme $C$ of finite type and dimension at most
one over an algebraically closed field,

$$
H^2(C_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_m)=0.
$$

Neither connectedness nor properness is required. By
[lemma-cohomology-multiplicative-group--5], this says that $\operatorname{Br}(C)=0$.

Let $C$ be an integral separated scheme of finite type and dimension at
most one over an algebraically closed field $k$. Its function field
$k(C)$ is $C_1$: every homogeneous form of positive degree $d$ in more
than $d$ variables has a nonzero zero. Moreover,

$$
H^2(\operatorname{Spec}(k(C))_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_m)=0.
$$

*Shared context.* Let $C$ be a smooth separated curve of finite type over
an algebraically closed field, with dimension at most one. Some
statements below are made more generally for schemes $X$ and $Y$, on the
small étale site. The comparison of
Theorem [theorem-bounded-below-cohomology-comparison] relates étale
cohomology to the cohomology of $\nu_C^*\mathbf G_m$ on the pro-étale site.

Let $X$ be a smooth surface over an algebraically closed field
of characteristic $p$, or an étale limit with affine transition
maps of such surfaces. Let $D_1,D_2$ be regular divisors meeting
transversely at exactly one point $z$, and let

$$
j:X-D_2\hookrightarrow X,\qquad
j':X-(D_1\cup D_2)\hookrightarrow X-D_2.
$$

Let $\ell\ne p$, let $A$ be a finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring,
and let $N$ be a bounded complex of $A$-modules on $X-(D_1\cup D_2)$
with finite locally constant cohomology whose monodromy factors
through a finite $\ell$-group. Put $M=Rj_*j'_!N$. Then $M_z=0$, and
$M|_{D_2-z}$ has finite locally constant cohomology. If $D_2$ is
connected, then for every closed geometric point $w\in D_2-z$ the
restriction map

$$
R\Gamma(D_2,M|_{D_2})\longrightarrow M_w
$$

is zero in $D(A)$.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $\ell$ be a prime
invertible in $k$. Let $X$ be a regular, locally noetherian $k$-scheme
which is a smooth surface, or a cofiltered limit of smooth surfaces
with affine étale transition maps. Let $D_1,D_2$ be regular divisors
whose scheme-theoretic intersection is the reduced point $z$ and is a
regular closed subscheme of codimension two in $X$. Write

$$
j:X-D_2\hookrightarrow X,\qquad
j':X-(D_1\cup D_2)\hookrightarrow X-D_2.
$$

Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring in which $\ell$ is nilpotent,
and let $N$ be a bounded complex of étale sheaves of $A$-modules on
$X-(D_1\cup D_2)$. Assume that, for each $n$, there is a finite étale
Galois cover with group a finite $\ell$-group on which $H^n(N)$ becomes
the constant sheaf associated to a finite $A$-module. Put $M=Rj_*j'_!N$.
Then $M_{\bar z}=0$ for every geometric point $\bar z$ over $z$, and
$H^n(M|_{D_2-z})$ is finite locally constant for every $n\in\mathbf Z$.

attrs.title: Vanishing at the corner and local constancy along the punctured divisor

objects.body:
With $X,D_1,D_2,z,A,N$ and $M$ as in
[lemma-cohomology-near-two-transverse-divisors--1], assume that $D_2$ is
connected. For every geometric point
$\bar w:\Spec\Omega\to D_2$ with $\Omega$ separably closed and image
different from $z$, the restriction map

$$
R\Gamma(D_2,M|_{D_2})\longrightarrow M_{\bar w}
$$

is zero in $D(A)$.

Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring, let $S$ be a
Noetherian scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let
$p:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ be the projection. The unit
$\Lambda_S\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}$ and the class
$c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1))$ define an isomorphism

$$
\sigma_S:\Lambda_S\oplus\Lambda_S(-1)[-2]
\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}
\quad\text{in }D^+(S_{\acute{e}t},\Lambda),
\tag{6.4}
$$

compatible with base change in the sense that for $g:S'\to S$ with $S'$
Noetherian, the base change map $g^*Rp_*\Lambda\to Rp'_*\Lambda$ carries $g^*\sigma_S$ to $\sigma_{S'}$. Let

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_p:Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]\longrightarrow\Lambda_S
\tag{6.5}
$$

be the morphism given by the projection
onto the summand $\Lambda_S$ of the twist of $\sigma_S$.
Then $\operatorname{Tr}_p$ is compatible with every Noetherian base
change.

$$
X'_m=Y\times_{\Phi_Y^m,Y,f}X,
\quad p_m:X'_m\to X,\quad f'_m:X'_m\to Y,
\quad r_m=(f,\Phi_X^m):X\to X'_m,
$$

where $p_m$ and $f'_m$ are the two projections.

1. The relative Frobenius $r_m$ is a finite universal homeomorphism,
   $p_mr_m=\Phi_X^m$ and $f'_mr_m=f$, and there are natural isomorphisms
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \theta_{f,m}:(\Phi_Y^m)^*Rf_!K
   &\simeq Rf'_{m!}p_m^*K
   \xrightarrow{Rf'_{m!}\eta_{r_m}}
   Rf'_{m!}Rr_{m*}r_m^*p_m^*K\\
   &\simeq Rf_!(\Phi_X^m)^*K,
   \end{aligned}
   $$

2. For a Frobenius correspondence $\psi:\Phi_X^*K\to K$ on

Let $G$ be an algebraic group.

1. $G$ has finitely many connected components. Its
   identity component $G^\circ$ is an open, closed, irreducible normal
   subgroup, the other components are its cosets, and
   $\operatorname{Lie}(G^\circ)=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$.
2. The image of a homomorphism $G\to G'$ of algebraic groups is a
   closed subgroup of $G'$.
3. If $G$ is connected and $K\subseteq G$ is a closed subgroup scheme
   with $\operatorname{Lie}(K)=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$, then $K=G$.

Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian affine scheme with function field
$k(S)$, and let $Y\to S$ be projective. Choose a finite affine open
cover $Y=\bigcup_\alpha Y_\alpha$ and closed immersions
$Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{m_\alpha}_S$ with
$m_\alpha\geq1$, and write $t_{\alpha r}:Y_\alpha\to\mathbf A^1_S$
($1\le r\le m_\alpha$) for the coordinate functions.

1. If $X\subset Y$ is open and $\dim X_{k(S)}\leq n$, then for
   every $\alpha,r$ the generic fibre of

   $n-1$.

   each $\alpha,r$, and let

   G=\bigcup_{\alpha,r}
   t_{\alpha r}^{-1}(V_{\alpha r})\subset Y.

   is finite over $S$.

point of $\mathbf A^1_S$, then

$$
\dim t^{-1}(\eta')+1\leq\dim X_{k(S)}.
$$

Here the fibres are scheme-theoretic and the dimensions are Krull
dimensions of the underlying spaces, with $\dim\emptyset=-\infty$.

   factors through a finite $\ell$-group.

Let $U_0/\mathbf F_q$ be a smooth geometrically connected curve, let
$\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$, and let $V$ be its
geometric generic fibre, a representation of the geometric fundamental
group $\pi_1(U)$.  There are canonical
Frobenius-equivariant identifications

$$
H^0(U,\mathcal F)=V^{\pi_1(U)},\qquad
H_c^2(U,\mathcal F)=V_{\pi_1(U)}(-1).
$$

There is no compactly supported cohomology outside degrees $0,1,2$.
If $U_0$ is affine, $H_c^0(U,\mathcal F)=0$.
If $\mathcal F$ is punctually of weights $\le a$, the weights of $H^0$
are at most $a$ and those of $H_c^2$ at most $a+2$.  If $\mathcal F$
is pure of weight $a$, the two groups, when nonzero, are pure of weights
$a$ and $a+2$, respectively.

Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f:W'\to W$ be a finite étale
morphism of schemes, and let $n\in\mathbf N$. Suppose that, for every
separably closed field $\Omega$ and every geometric point
$\bar w:\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega)\to W$, the geometric fibre of $f$
over $\bar w$ has $n$ points. For every $L\in D(W_{\acute{e}t},A)$, the
pullback map

$$
p:R\Gamma(W,L)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(W',f^{-1}L)
$$

admits a trace $t:R\Gamma(W',f^{-1}L)\to R\Gamma(W,L)$ in $D(A)$ such
that $t\circ p=n\,\operatorname{id}_{R\Gamma(W,L)}$. There is no invertibility assumption on $n$, and $L$ need
not be bounded. In particular, if $n$ is invertible in $A$, then
$n^{-1}t$ is a left inverse of $p$.

Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $M_1,M_2,M'_1,M'_2\in D(A)$, and
let

$$
r:M_1\to M_2,\qquad r':M'_1\to M'_2,\qquad
p_1:M_1\to M'_1,\qquad p_2:M_2\to M'_2
$$

satisfy $p_2\circ r=r'\circ p_1$. Suppose there are a morphism
$t:M'_2\to M_2$ and an integer $n$ whose image in $A$ is invertible,
such that $t\circ p_2=n\,\operatorname{id}_{M_2}$. If $r'=0$, then
$r=0$.

In particular, let $n$ be invertible in $A$, and let $p$ and $t$ be the
pullback map and the trace of [lemma-descent-vanishing-finite-etale--1].
Taking $r=\alpha$, $p_1=\operatorname{id}_M$, $r'=p\circ\alpha$ and
$p_2=p$ shows that a morphism $\alpha:M\to R\Gamma(W,L)$ in $D(A)$ is
zero if $p\circ\alpha=0$.

immersion with reduced closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, and
suppose that $bi:Z\to S$ is finite.

1. If $K\in D^+(Y_{\acute{e}t},\Fell)$, $j^*K\in\Dbc(U,\Fell)$, and
   $Rb_*K\in\Dbc(S,\Fell)$, then $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Fell)$.
2. If $\varphi:K\to K'$ is a morphism in $D^+(Y_{\acute{e}t},\Fell)$ such
   that $j^*\varphi$ and

   isomorphism.

be a morphism of schemes, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ and
$i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion and a closed immersion whose
images are complementary. Suppose that $bi:Z\to S$ is finite. We work on
the étale sites; $Z$ may have any closed subscheme structure with this
underlying closed subset. The schemes and the coefficient ring are
arbitrary unless further hypotheses are stated in the detail.

attrs.title: Detection by a proper direct image

objects.body:
In the setting of Proposition [proposition-central-element-arithmetic-monodromy-group], let $Q$
be a nonzero subquotient of a tensor construction on $V$ on which the
element $z$ acts by a scalar $c_Q$. Then

$$
\operatorname{dw}_\iota(Q)=\frac{\lambda_\iota(c_Q)}{N}.
$$

attrs.title: Determinant weight from a central scalar

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field, let $W$ be a group with a surjective homomorphism
$\deg:W\to\mathbf Z$ and a chosen element $s$ of degree one, and let
$\rho:W\to\GL(k^n)$ be a representation. Put $P=\ker\deg$, and let
$H\subseteq G$ be the Zariski closures of $\rho(P)$ and $\rho(W)$,
as in [definition-monodromy-groups]. Let
$\lambda:k^\times\to(\R,+)$ be a homomorphism. Suppose that $N>0$ is
an integer and that

$$
z=h\rho(s)^N,\qquad h\in H(k),\qquad z\in Z(G(k)),
$$

so that $(N,z)$ is a positive central pair of the form supplied by
[proposition-central-element-arithmetic-monodromy-group].

Let $U\subsetneq S\subseteq k^n$ be $W$-stable subspaces, and put
$Q=S/U$. Assume that the determinant character $\delta_Q$ has finite
image on $P$ and that $c_Q\in k^\times$ satisfies
$zx-c_Qx\in U$ for every $x\in S$. With the determinant weight defined
as in [definition-determinant-weight], using $\lambda$ and $s$, we have

$$
\operatorname{dw}_\lambda(Q)
=\frac{\lambda(\delta_Q(s))}{\dim_k Q}
=\frac{\lambda(c_Q)}{N}.
$$

For the Weil representations of
[proposition-central-element-arithmetic-monodromy-group], take
$k=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and $\lambda=\lambda_\iota$; the hypothesis
on $\delta_Q$ holds by [corollary-determinant-weights]. Transporting
$(N,z)$ along a tensor construction as in
[proposition-central-element-arithmetic-monodromy-group--2], the formula
gives $\operatorname{dw}_\iota(Q)=\lambda_\iota(c_Q)/N$ for every nonzero
subquotient $Q$ of a tensor construction on $V$ on which $z$ acts by a
scalar $c_Q$.

$V\subseteq M$ be a quasi-compact open with a compactification
$V\subseteq Y$ over $S$. There are a $V$-admissible blow-up $Y'\to Y$,

attrs.title: Extending a graph from a compactification

objects.body:
Let $S$ be qcqs, let $u:M\to S$ be separated of finite type, and let
$j:V\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion of a quasi-compact open. Fix a
compactification $V\xrightarrow{i}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ of $u\circ j$.
There are an $i(V)$-admissible blow-up $b:Y'\to Y$, an open
$k:V'\hookrightarrow Y'$, a proper map $\psi:V'\to M$, and an open
immersion $v:V\to V'$ such that

$$
b\circ k\circ v=i,\qquad
\psi\circ v=j,\qquad
u\circ\psi=g\circ b\circ k.
$$

Moreover, $\psi^{-1}(V)=v(V)$, and the restriction
$\psi^{-1}(V)\to V$ of $\psi$ is an isomorphism.

Let $q:P\to T$ be a proper morphism of qcqs schemes, let $V\subseteq T$
be a quasi-compact open, and let $F\subseteq V$ be closed. Suppose that
$q$ is an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of $F$ in $V$.
After a $V$-admissible blow-up, the strict transform of $q$ is an
isomorphism over a neighbourhood of the closure of $F$.

attrs.title: Extending an isomorphism over the closure of a closed subset

objects.body:
Let $T$ be qcqs, let $q:P\to T$ be proper, let $V\subseteq T$ be a
quasi-compact open, and let $F\subseteq V$ be closed in $V$. Let
$N\subseteq T$ be an open containing $F$ such that $q$ is an
isomorphism over $N$.

Then there is a $V$-admissible blow-up $b:T'\to T$ with the following
property: if $q':P'\to T'$ is the strict transform of $q$, there is an
open $N'\subseteq T'$ such that

$$
\overline{b^{-1}(F)}\subseteq N',\qquad
q'|_{N'}:(q')^{-1}(N')\xrightarrow{\sim}N'.
$$

Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open in a smooth
geometrically connected affine curve, let $F$ be lisse on $U_0$, and
put $V=F_{\bar\eta}$. Then $H_c^i(C,j_*F)=0$ for $i\ne1,2$, and there
is a canonical identification

$$
H_c^2(C,j_*F)=V_{\pi_1(U)}(-1).
$$

If $F$ is pure of weight $w$, the group in degree two, when nonzero,
is pure of weight $w+2$.

attrs.title: The extreme degrees on an affine curve

objects.body:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a quasi-compact open immersion into
a smooth affine curve over $\Fq$, and let $F$ be a lisse
$\Qbarl$-Weil sheaf on $U_0$, with $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}\Fq$.
Write $U$ and $C$ for the base changes to $\Fbar$. Then
$H_c^r(C,j_*F)=0$ for every integer $r<0$ or $r>2$.

If moreover $C_0$ is geometrically connected and $j$ is dense, then
$H_c^0(C,j_*F)=0$. Thus in this case
$H_c^r(C,j_*F)=0$ for $r\ne1,2$.

attrs.title: Vanishing outside degrees one and two

objects.body:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open in a smooth
geometrically connected affine curve over $\Fq$, and let $F$ be a
lisse $\Qbarl$-Weil sheaf on $U_0$, with
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}\Fq$. Write $U$ and $C$ for the base
changes to $\Fbar$, and put

$$
W=H^0(U,F^\vee)^\vee,
$$

with the dual Frobenius action. There is a Frobenius-equivariant
isomorphism

$$
H_c^2(C,j_*F)\simeq W(-1).
$$

Here $W$ is the space $V_{\pi_1(U)}$ of geometric coinvariants of
$V=F_{\bar\eta}$, since $H^0(U,F^\vee)=(V^\vee)^{\pi_1(U)}$ is the dual
of $V_{\pi_1(U)}$; the twist $(-1)$ multiplies its Frobenius by $q$.

Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open in a smooth
geometrically connected affine curve over $\Fq$, and let $F$ be a
lisse $\Qbarl$-Weil sheaf on $U_0$, with
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}\Fq$. Fix
$\iota:\Qbarl\hookrightarrow\C$ and $w\in\R$.
If $F$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, then
$H_c^2(C,j_*F)$, where $C=C_0\times_{\Fq}\Fbar$, is
$\iota$-pure of weight $w+2$. This includes the zero space, for
which the eigenvalue condition is vacuous.

finitely filtered complex on $X$ with underlying complex $K$ and graded
pieces $K_a$ in $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,A)$. There is a morphism of filtered complexes

$$
\operatorname{tr}_F:
\cHom_F(c_2^*\mathcal K,c_1^!\mathcal K)\longrightarrow
Ri_{c*}\omega_{\Fix(c)},
$$

with the target in weight zero, whose underlying morphism is the trace
morphism for $K$, and whose restriction to $F^0$ factors through

$$
\operatorname{gr}^0\cHom_F(c_2^*\mathcal K,c_1^!\mathcal K)
\simeq\bigoplus_a\cHom(c_2^*K_a,c_1^!K_a)
$$

by a map whose restriction to the summand $a$ is the trace morphism
for $K_a$.

Let $V$ have a finite filtration preserved by an automorphism $u$.
Then

$$
\det(1-Tu\mid V)=\prod_a\det(1-Tu\mid\operatorname{gr}_aV).
$$

In particular, the eigenvalues, with algebraic multiplicity, are the
union of the eigenvalues on the graded pieces. If the eigenvalues of
$u$ on $V$ are $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d$, then those on $V^\vee$ are
$\alpha_i^{-1}$, and those on $\bigwedge^rV$ are
$\alpha_{i_1}\cdots\alpha_{i_r}$ for $i_1<\cdots<i_r$.
If $v$ on $V'$ has eigenvalues $\beta_j$, those of $u\otimes v$ are
$\alpha_i\beta_j$.

Let $K$ be a field, $V$ a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space, and
$u:V\to V$ a linear endomorphism. Let $(F_i)_{i\geq0}$ be subspaces
preserved by $u$, with $F_0=0$, $F_n=V$, and $F_i\subseteq F_{i+1}$
for $0\leq i<n$. Write $u_i$ for the induced endomorphism of
$\operatorname{gr}_iV=F_{i+1}/F_i$. Then

$$
\det(T-u\mid V)=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}
\det(T-u_i\mid\operatorname{gr}_iV).
$$

Reversing these characteristic polynomials gives the identity for
$\det(1-Tu\mid V)$. Invertibility of $u$ is not required.

Let $K$ be algebraically closed and let $V$, $u$, and the filtration
be as in [lemma-filtrations-spectra--1]. Write $E(u)$ for the multiset
of roots of $\det(T-u\mid V)$, and similarly for the endomorphisms
$u_i$ of the graded pieces. Then

$$
E(u)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}E(u_i).
$$

Thus the eigenvalues, with algebraic multiplicity, are the union of
the eigenvalues on the graded pieces.

Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field, $V$ a finite-dimensional
$K$-vector space, and $u$ an automorphism of $V$. On $V^\vee$ take
the contragredient action $(u^{-1})^\vee$, sending
$\varphi$ to $\varphi\circ u^{-1}$. If the eigenvalues of $u$ are
$\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d$, counted with algebraic multiplicity,
then the eigenvalues of this action on $V^\vee$, with the same
multiplicities, are $\alpha_1^{-1},\ldots,\alpha_d^{-1}$.

Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field, $V$ a finite-dimensional
$K$-vector space, and $u$ a linear endomorphism of $V$ with eigenvalues
$\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d$, counted with algebraic multiplicity.
For every integer $r\geq0$, the eigenvalues of $\bigwedge^r u$ on
$\bigwedge^rV$ are

$$
\alpha_{i_1}\cdots\alpha_{i_r}
\qquad(1\leq i_1<\cdots<i_r\leq d),
$$

one for each choice of indices, with repetitions retained. For $r=0$
this is the single eigenvalue $1$; for $r>d$ the multiset is empty.

Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field, $V$ and $V'$ finite-dimensional
$K$-vector spaces, and $u:V\to V$ and $v:V'\to V'$ linear
endomorphisms. If their eigenvalues, counted with algebraic
multiplicity, are $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d$ and
$\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_e$, then the eigenvalues of $u\otimes v$ on
$V\otimes_K V'$ are $\alpha_i\beta_j$ for all $1\leq i\leq d$ and
$1\leq j\leq e$, with repetitions retained.

attrs.title: A finite cover of projective space

objects.body:
For a scheme $S$, realize the powers of the projective line as the tower

$$
X_0=S,\qquad X_{k+1}=\mathbf P^1_{X_k},
$$

so that $X_k\simeq(\mathbf P^1_S)^k$, and let $p_k:X_k\to S$ be the
composite of its projections, with $p_0=\operatorname{id}_S$. Let $k\geq0$ and write
$\pi:\mathbf P^k_S\to S$ for the projection.

The symmetric product morphism

$$
\sigma_k:X_k\longrightarrow\mathbf P^k_S,
$$

constructed recursively by multiplying binary linear forms, is finite
and surjective, and satisfies

$$
\pi\circ\sigma_k=p_k.
$$

Let $W_0$ be a dense open of $\mathbf P^1_{k_0}$, and let $F$ be a

infinity, and a surjection

$$
H_c^1(V,G)\twoheadrightarrow H_c^1(W,F)

that commutes with the geometric Frobenius of $k_m$.

objects.body:
Let $u:V\to W$ be finite. For an abelian sheaf $F$ and a geometric point
$\bar w:\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega)\to W$, with $\Omega$ algebraically
closed, one has

$$
(u_*F)_{\bar w}
\simeq \prod_{\substack{\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega)\to V\\
u\bar v=\bar w}}F_{\bar v}.
$$

The product is finite. The functor $u_*$ from abelian sheaves on
$V_{\acute{e}t}$ to abelian sheaves on $W_{\acute{e}t}$ is exact, and its formation
commutes with arbitrary base change. Consequently, for
every base change $W'\to W$ and every constant coefficient ring
$\Lambda$, the derived base change map
(4.3) is an isomorphism
for every $K\in D^+(V_{\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$.

Let $A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category, and let $u:V\to W$ be finite. For an $A$-valued sheaf $F$ on
$V_{\acute{e}t}$ and a geometric point
$\bar w:\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega)\to W$, with $\Omega$ algebraically
closed, one has

$$
(u_*F)_{\bar w}
\simeq \prod_{\substack{\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega)\to V\\
u\bar v=\bar w}}F_{\bar v}.

maps on germs. The product is finite. In particular, this applies to
abelian sheaves and to sheaves of modules over a constant coefficient ring.

Let $\psi$ be nontrivial, let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$
be a dense open, put $U=U_0\otimes_{k_0}\bar k_0$, and let $M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $U_0$ with no geometric irreducible
constituent of the form $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_{U}$ for $a\in\bar k_0$.
Fix a dense open $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{1\vee}_{k_0}$,
a lisse Weil sheaf $M'$ on $U'_0$, and an isomorphism
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi((j_*M)[1])\simeq(j'_*M')[1]$, as in
[proposition-fourier-transform-middle-extension]. No assumption on the
weights of $M$ is needed here; in [lemma-fourier-transform-boundary-sequence--2], $M$ is moreover pure of weight $w$.

Put $B=j_*M/j_!M$. There are Weil sheaves $G$ and $B'$ on the dual line
and isomorphisms
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!M)\simeq G$ and
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(B)\simeq B'[1]$, together with a short exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow B'\longrightarrow G
\overset{g}{\longrightarrow} j'_*M'\longrightarrow0.
$$

Under the corresponding isomorphisms
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!M[1])\simeq G[1]$ and
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_*M[1])\simeq(j'_*M')[1]$, the map $g[1]$
is the Fourier transform of the canonical map $j_!M[1]\to j_*M[1]$.

The sheaf $B'$ is lisse on the entire dual line and has weights at
most $w$.

Let $X$ be a nonempty connected normal scheme of finite type over a
field. Let $p:Y\to X$ be separated and étale. Suppose that for every
valuation ring $V$, with fraction field $K$, every commutative diagram

$$
\begin{CD}
\operatorname{Spec}K @>>> Y\\
@VVV @VVpV\\
\operatorname{Spec}V @>>> X
\end{CD}
$$

has a lift $\operatorname{Spec}V\to Y$. Then every connected component
of $Y$ is finite étale and surjective over $X$.

For a field $K$ and $C(T)=\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n\in K[[T]]$, the
following conditions are equivalent:

1. $C(T)$ is rational and regular at zero;
2. the finite submatrices of $(c_{r+s})_{r,s\geq0}$ have bounded rank;
3. the span of the rows $R_j=(c_{j+s})_{s\geq0}$ is finite-dimensional.

If $K\subset K'$ and $C$ has coefficients in $K$, rationality over
$K'$ implies rationality over $K$.

Let $K\subset K'$ be fields and $C(T)\in K[[T]]$. Write $C_{K'}$
for the same series viewed in $K'[[T]]$. Then the following conditions
are equivalent:

1. there are $P',Q'\in K'[T]$ with $Q'(0)=1$ and $C_{K'}Q'=P'$;
2. there are $P,Q\in K[T]$ with $Q(0)=1$ and $CQ=P$.

Thus rationality, with regularity at zero, is preserved and reflected
by extension of the coefficient field.

The thick category $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$ is essentially small.

A small skeleton of $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$ is a set of compact generators of $\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E))$.
A small skeleton of $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},E)$ is a set of compact generators of $\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},E))$.

A small skeleton of $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ is a set of compact generators of $\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell))$.
*Shared context.* Use the full subcategories and localizing closures defined in the reference. The integral and field clauses include $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Q_\ell$ through $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

If $V$ is a semisimple $W(U_0)$-representation, then

$$
G^\circ=Z(G^\circ)^\circ H^\circ.
$$

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let
$H\subseteq G\subseteq\GL(k^n)$ be closed subgroup schemes. Put

$$
R=k[\varepsilon,\eta]/(\varepsilon^2,\eta^2).
$$

Suppose that every commutator of two elements of $G(R)$ lies in $H(R)$,
and that the defining representation of $G^\circ(k)$ on $k^n$ is
semisimple. Then every $g\in G^\circ(k)$ can be written as

$$
g=th,\qquad t\in Z(G^\circ)^\circ(k),\quad h\in H^\circ(k).
$$

In particular, if $V$ is a semisimple $W(U_0)$-representation with
monodromy groups $H\subseteq G$ as in [definition-monodromy-groups], then
$G^\circ=Z(G^\circ)^\circ H^\circ$.

Let $K\in D^+(X_{\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$. The base change map is the identity for an
identity square, and is compatible with horizontal and vertical pasting
of commutative squares, in particular of cartesian squares. More
explicitly, if $h:Y''\to Y'$ is a second base change, completed by maps
$h':X''\to X'$ and $f'':X''\to Y''$ to a commutative square with
$f'h'=hf''$, the base change map for the pasted square, with bottom map
$gh$, is the composite

$$
h^*g^*Rf_*K
\longrightarrow
h^*Rf'_*g'^*K
\longrightarrow
Rf''_*h'^*g'^*K
$$

of $h^*$ applied to the base change map of (4.1) and the
base change map of the second square, under the canonical composition
isomorphisms.

For composable maps $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ and a map
$h:Z'\to Z$, let $g':Y'\to Z'$, $h_Y:Y'\to Y$ and $f':X'\to Y'$,
$h_X:X'\to X$ complete $g$, $h$ and $f$, $h_Y$ to commutative squares
(for instance $Y'=Y\times_ZZ'$ and $X'=X\times_ZZ'$). Then the base change
map for the pasted square with left map $g'f'$ and right map $gf$ is the
composite

$$
h^*Rg_*Rf_*K
\longrightarrow
Rg'_*h_Y^*Rf_*K
\longrightarrow
Rg'_*Rf'_*h_X^*K
$$

of the base change map for $g$ at $Rf_*K$ and $Rg'_*$ applied to the
base change map for $f$ at $K$.

Let $A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category, for instance the category of
$\Lambda$-modules, let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, and let
$K\in D^+(X_{\acute{e}t},A)$. For the commutative square with vertical
maps $f,f$ and horizontal maps $\mathrm{id}_X,\mathrm{id}_Y$, the base
change map of [definition-derived-base-change-map] is the composite

$$
(\mathrm{id}_Y)^*Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(\mathrm{id}_X)^*K,
$$

where the arrows come from the canonical identity isomorphisms of
pullback. This is an equality of natural transformations in $K$; under
these identifications the base change map is the identity.

Let $A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category, for instance the category of
$\Lambda$-modules, and let $K\in D^+(X_{\acute{e}t},A)$. Let
$f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$ and $g':X'\to X$ form a
commutative square with $fg'=gf'$. If $h:Y''\to Y'$ is a second base
change, completed by maps
$h':X''\to X'$ and $f'':X''\to Y''$ to a commutative square with
$f'h'=hf''$, the base change map for the pasted square, with bottom map
$gh$, is the composite

$$
(gh)^*Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{\sim}
h^*g^*Rf_*K
\longrightarrow
h^*Rf'_*g'^*K
\longrightarrow
Rf''_*h'^*g'^*K
\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rf''_*(g'h')^*K
$$

of the canonical composition isomorphisms, $h^*$ applied to the base
change map of the first square, and the base change map of the second
square, as in [definition-derived-base-change-map]. This is an equality
of natural transformations in $K$. Only commutativity of the squares
is required.

Let $A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category, for instance the category of
$\Lambda$-modules, and let $K\in D^+(X_{\acute{e}t},A)$. For composable maps
$X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ and a map
$h:Z'\to Z$, let $g':Y'\to Z'$, $h_Y:Y'\to Y$ and $f':X'\to Y'$,
$h_X:X'\to X$ complete $g$, $h$ and $f$, $h_Y$ to commutative squares
(for instance $Y'=Y\times_ZZ'$ and $X'=X\times_ZZ'$). Then the base change
map for the pasted square with left map $g'f'$ and right map $gf$ is the
composite

$$
h^*R(gf)_*K
\xrightarrow{\sim}
h^*Rg_*Rf_*K
\longrightarrow
Rg'_*h_Y^*Rf_*K
\longrightarrow
Rg'_*Rf'_*h_X^*K
\xrightarrow{\sim}
R(g'f')_*h_X^*K
$$

of the canonical composition isomorphisms for derived direct image,
the base change map for $g$ at $Rf_*K$, and $Rg'_*$ applied to the
base change map for $f$ at $K$, as in [definition-derived-base-change-map].
This is an equality of natural transformations in $K$. Only
commutativity of the squares is required.
*Shared context.* Let $K\in D^+(X_{\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$. The statements apply to commutative squares as in the reference, hence also to cartesian squares.

Let $Q^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of finite free
$\mathcal O_E$-modules, and let $\pi_E^e$ kill the torsion of
$H^{q+1}(Q^\bullet)$. Then for $m\ge n+e$

$$
\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^q(Q^\bullet/\pi_E^m)\to
H^q(Q^\bullet/\pi_E^n)\bigr)
=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^q(Q^\bullet)\to
H^q(Q^\bullet/\pi_E^n)\bigr).
$$

attrs.title: Images of cohomology at finite levels (1)

objects.body:
Suppose $q\geq1$ and $\mathrm{BC}(g,n,q-1)$ holds. For every square
obtained by base change as in the definition of $\mathrm{BC}$ and every
sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules $M$ on $Z_{\acute{e}t}$, the base change map
$b_M^q:g^{-1}R^qf_*M\to R^qf'_*g'^{-1}M$ in degree $q$ is injective. An inclusion
$M\hookrightarrow N$ induces

$$
\operatorname{coker}(b_M^q)
\hookrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(b_N^q).
$$

For an embedding $M\hookrightarrow I$ with $I$ injective in the
category of étale sheaves of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules, the cokernel of
$b_M^q$ embeds into $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I$.

attrs.title: Injectivity of the base change map in degree $q$

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $g:Y'\to Y$ a morphism of schemes,
and $q\in\mathbf Z$ with $q\geq1$. For a cartesian square

$$
\begin{CD}
Z' @>{g'}>> Z\\
@V{f'}VV @VV{f}V\\
Y' @>{g}>> Y
\end{CD}
$$

and a sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $Z_{\acute{e}t}$, write

$$
b_M^r:H^r(g^*Rf_*(M[0]))\longrightarrow H^r(Rf'_*g'^*(M[0]))
$$

for the map on cohomology induced by
[definition-derived-base-change-map]. Since inverse image is exact, its
source and target are written $g^{-1}R^rf_*M$ and
$R^rf'_*g'^{-1}M$.

Suppose that $b_M^{q-1}$ is an isomorphism for every such square with
$f$ qcqs and every sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda$-modules. Then $b_M^q$ is
injective for every such square with $f$ qcqs and every $M$.

attrs.title: Injectivity of the base change map in degree $q$ (1)

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $g:Y'\to Y$ a morphism of schemes,
and $q\in\mathbf Z$ with $q\geq1$. Suppose that degree-$(q-1)$ base
change along $g$ is an isomorphism for every qcqs morphism $f:Z\to Y$
and every sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $Z_{\acute{e}t}$.

For such an $f$, form $Z'=Y'\times_Y Z$ with projections $g':Z'\to Z$
and $f':Z'\to Y'$. Write $b_M^r$ for the map on degree-$r$ cohomology
of [definition-derived-base-change-map] evaluated at $M[0]$. Every
inclusion $M\hookrightarrow N$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on
$Z_{\acute{e}t}$ induces an injection

$$
\operatorname{coker}(b_M^q)
\hookrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(b_N^q).
$$

attrs.title: Injectivity of the base change map in degree $q$ (2)

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $g:Y'\to Y$ a morphism of schemes,
and $q\in\mathbf Z$ with $q\geq1$. Suppose that degree-$(q-1)$ base
change along $g$ is an isomorphism for every qcqs morphism $f:Z\to Y$
and every sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $Z_{\acute{e}t}$.

For such an $f$, form $Z'=Y'\times_Y Z$ with projections $g':Z'\to Z$
and $f':Z'\to Y'$. Write $b_M^r$ for the map on degree-$r$ cohomology
of [definition-derived-base-change-map] evaluated at $M[0]$.
For an embedding $M\hookrightarrow I$ into an injective sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules on $Z_{\acute{e}t}$, the natural map
$R^qf'_*g'^{-1}M\to R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I$ induces an injection

$$
\operatorname{coker}(b_M^q)\hookrightarrow R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I.
$$

Here $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I$ denotes $H^q(Rf'_*g'^*(I[0]))$.

attrs.title: Injectivity of the base change map in degree $q$ (3)

objects.body:
Assume $\mathrm{BC}(g,n,q-1)$. A failure of base change in degree $q$
persists after an integral surjective change of the source of the
morphism along which we take direct image. It also persists after an integral
change of the base through which this morphism factors.

attrs.title: Integral changes of source and base

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of
schemes, and let $q\geq1$ be an integer. Assume that for every qcqs
morphism $h:W\to T$ and every sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on
$W_{\acute{e}t}$, the base change map along $g$ in degree $q-1$ is an
isomorphism.

Let $f:Z\to T$ be qcqs, let $M$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on
$Z_{\acute{e}t}$, and let $\pi:\widetilde Z\to Z$ be integral and
surjective. Write $Z'=T'\times_TZ$, with projections $g_Z:Z'\to Z$ and
$f':Z'\to T'$, and let

$$
b^q_{f,M}:g^{-1}R^qf_*M\longrightarrow R^qf'_*g_Z^{-1}M
$$

be the degree-$q$ map of Definition [definition-derived-base-change-map].
If $b^q_{f\pi,\pi^{-1}M}$ is an isomorphism, then $b^q_{f,M}$ is an
isomorphism. Equivalently, a failure for $f$ and $M$ persists for
$f\pi$ and $\pi^{-1}M$.

attrs.title: Integral changes of source and base (1)

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $g:Y'_T\to T$, $\pi:T'\to T$
and $f_1:Z\to T'$ be morphisms of schemes, with $\pi$ integral. Put
$f=\pi\circ f_1$ and $Y'_{T'}=Y'_T\times_TT'$, and let
$Z'=Y'_{T'}\times_{T'}Z\simeq Y'_T\times_TZ$. Write
$g_1:Y'_{T'}\to T'$, $\pi':Y'_{T'}\to Y'_T$, $g_Z:Z'\to Z$ and
$f'_1:Z'\to Y'_{T'}$ for the projections, and put $f'=\pi'\circ f'_1$.

For every integer $q$ and every sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda$-modules on
$Z_{\acute{e}t}$, the base change maps

$$
b^q_{f,M}:g^{-1}R^qf_*M\longrightarrow R^qf'_*g_Z^{-1}M,
\qquad
b^q_{f_1,M}:g_1^{-1}R^qf_{1*}M\longrightarrow R^qf'_{1*}g_Z^{-1}M
$$

satisfy

$$
b^q_{f,M}\text{ is an isomorphism}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
b^q_{f_1,M}\text{ is an isomorphism}.
$$

Thus a failure persists in either direction. No lower-degree base change
hypothesis or qcqs hypothesis on $f_1$ is required.

attrs.title: Integral changes of source and base (2)

objects.body:
Let $\lambda$ be a linear form on $\mathbf A^r$ over an algebraically
closed field of characteristic $p$. Then

$$
R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^r,\lambda^*\mathcal L_\psi)
\simeq
\begin{cases}
E(-r)[-2r],&\lambda=0,\\
0,&\lambda\ne0.
\end{cases}
$$

For $\lambda=0$, the isomorphism is the trace map for cohomology with
compact support.

attrs.title: The integral of a linear character

objects.body: If $\lambda=0$, then $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^r,\lambda^*\mathcal L_\psi)\simeq E(-r)[-2r]$.
If $\lambda\neq0$, then $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^r,\lambda^*\mathcal L_\psi)=0$.
For $\lambda=0$, the specified isomorphism is the trace map for compactly supported cohomology.
*Shared context.* Let $\lambda$ be a linear form on $\mathbf A^r$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, with the specified sheaf $\mathcal L_\psi$.

Let $W$ be an affine weakly contractible scheme, let
$K\in D(W_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$ be derived complete, and let $P^\bullet$
be a bounded complex of finite free $\mathcal O_E$-modules. Suppose that
for every $n\geq1$ there is an isomorphism
$(P^\bullet/\pi_E^n)_W\simeq K_n$ in $D(W_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)$.
Then $K\simeq\mathcal O_{E,W}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}P^\bullet$.

1. Restriction of scalars along the map from the constant sheaf
   $\mathcal O_E$ to $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ is an equivalence between the
   derived complete objects of $D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$ and the derived
   complete complexes of modules over the constant sheaf $\mathcal O_E$.
2. An object $K$ of $D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$ lies in
   $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ if and only if its restriction of scalars lies in
   $\Dc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.
3. $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$ is preserved by
   $f^*:D(Y_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$
   for every morphism $f:X\to Y$, by

   and by
   $a_!:D(S_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$ for
   every locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$.
4. Every object of $\Dbc(X,E)$ is obtained by finitely many cones and
   shifts from objects $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$, where $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is
   a locally closed immersion and $L_0$ is a lisse
   $\mathcal O_{E,S}$-module that is locally free of finite rank. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ is obtained in
   the same way from the objects $\QbarX\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}a_!L_0$,
   for some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$.

Let $X$ be Noetherian and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite. Write $R$ for the
constant sheaf $\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_{E,X}$ and
$\operatorname{Res}:D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},B)\to D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},R)$
for restriction along $R\to B$. For every complex $K$, $K$ is derived
$\pi_E$-complete if and only if $\operatorname{Res} K$ is derived $\pi_E$-complete.
Moreover, restriction induces an equivalence of the full subcategories
of complete complexes. The composite of this equivalence with the target
inclusion is naturally isomorphic to restriction composed with the source
inclusion. No boundedness or constructibility is assumed.

attrs.title: Restriction of scalars on complete complexes

objects.body:
Let $X$ be Noetherian and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite. An object
$K\in D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_{E,X})$ belongs to
$\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ if and only if its restriction to the constant
sheaf $\mathcal O_E$ belongs to $\Dc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Here the latter
condition means derived completeness, constructible cohomology of the
derived first reduction, and finite Tor amplitude of that reduction.

Restriction induces an equivalence

$$
\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)\simeq\Dc(X,\mathcal O_E),
$$

compatible, up to natural isomorphism, with the inclusions into the ambient
derived categories and restriction of scalars.
For every morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^*_{\mathcal O_E}:D(Y_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$ preserves $\Dbc$.
The functor $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}$ sends pairs of objects of $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$ to $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$.
For every locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$, $a_{!,\mathcal O_E}$ sends $\Dbc(S_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$.

Every object of $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},E)$ is obtained by finitely many cones and shifts from $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$, where $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is locally closed and $L_0$ is a lisse $\mathcal O_{E,S}$-module locally free of finite rank.

attrs.title: Generators over a finite coefficient field

objects.body: Every object of $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ is obtained by finitely many cones and shifts from $\QbarX\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}a_!L_0$, with $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $a,L_0$ as in the preceding clause.

Let $K_E\in\Dbc(X,E)$ and let
$\psi_E:\Phi_X^*K_E\to K_E$ be any morphism. There
exist $K_0\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, an isomorphism
$K_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_E}E\simeq K_E$, an integer $N\geq0$, and a
Frobenius correspondence $\theta:\Phi_X^*K_0\to K_0$ such that

$$
\psi_E=\pi_E^{-N}(\theta\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_E}E).
$$

For every $m\geq1$ the operators of Definition [definition-frobenius-correspondences-their-operators]
satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{c_m}((\psi_E)_m)&=\pi_E^{-Nm}
\bigl(T_{c_m}(\theta_m)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr),\\
(\psi_E)_{m,\bar y}&=\pi_E^{-Nm}
\bigl(\theta_{m,\bar y}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\tag{12.2}
$$

attrs.title: Inverse image of the coefficient sheaves

objects.body:
For every condensed ring $\Lambda$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ for a
scheme $T$, as in Subsection [subsec-Coefficient-sheaves]. The canonical map

$$

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be a prime,
and let $E$ be a field that is an admissible coefficient ring, for instance $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $a:U\to V$ be a morphism of
separated schemes of finite type over $k$. For bounded constructible
$E$-complexes $A$ on $U$ and $B$ on $V$, the exceptional projection map

$$
Ra_!A\otimes B\longrightarrow Ra_!(A\otimes a^*B)
$$

is an isomorphism. Taking $a=f$, $A=K$ and $B=Rg_!L$, its inverse gives

$$
Rf_!(K\otimes f^*Rg_!L)\simeq Rf_!K\otimes Rg_!L.
$$

Taking $a=p_1$, $A=p_2^*L$ and $B=K$ instead, and using the symmetry
of the tensor product, gives

$$
Rp_{1!}(p_1^*K\otimes p_2^*L)\simeq K\otimes Rp_{1!}p_2^*L.
$$

The composite

$$
Rh_!(p_1^*K\otimes p_2^*L)
\simeq Rf_!(K\otimes Rp_{1!}p_2^*L)
\simeq Rf_!(K\otimes f^*Rg_!L)
\simeq Rf_!K\otimes Rg_!L
$$

of the projection formula for $p_1$, the base change isomorphism of
[lemma-kunneth-formula-compact-supports--2] and the projection formula
for $f$ is called the *Künneth isomorphism*
$Rh_!(K\boxtimes_SL)\simeq Rf_!K\otimes Rg_!L$.

linear functional $\lambda:\mathfrak l\to\Omega$ such that

$$
av=\lambda(a)v\quad(a\in\mathfrak l).

In particular $\lambda([\mathfrak l,\mathfrak l])=0$, since $[a,b]$ acts on $v$
by $\lambda(a)\lambda(b)-\lambda(b)\lambda(a)=0$.

Let $X_0$ be a quasi-separated scheme of finite type over $k_0=\Fq$,
let $j:U_0\to X_0$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, and let
$i:Z_0\to X_0$ be a closed immersion whose image is the complement
of the image of $j$. Fix a prime $\ell\nmid q$ and
$\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$.
For a constructible Weil $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf $G$ on
$X_0$ and $w\in\mathbf R$, if $j^*G$ and $i^*G$ are
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$, then $G$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$. In particular, if $j^*G$ and
$i^*G$ are $\iota$-mixed, then so is $G$.

Let (4.1) be a cartesian square, let $\Lambda$ be a discrete commutative
ring, and let $K\in D^+(X_{\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$. Suppose that $f$ and
$f'$ are qcqs. The comparison of inverse images and the isomorphisms of
Theorem [theorem-comparison-direct-images] give isomorphisms

$$
\alpha_K:\nu_{Y'}^*g_{\acute{e}t}^*Rf_{\acute{e}t,*}K
\xrightarrow{\sim}
g_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}^*Rf_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t,*}\nu_X^*K,
$$

$$
\beta_K:\nu_{Y'}^*Rf'_{\acute{e}t,*}g'^*_{\acute{e}t}K
\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rf'_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t,*}g'^*_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}\nu_X^*K.
$$

Here $\alpha_K$ first commutes $\nu^*$ with $g^*$ and then uses the
direct image comparison for $f$; $\beta_K$ first uses the direct image
comparison for $f'$ and then commutes $\nu^*$ with $g'^*$. All objects
are viewed in $D(Y'_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$, and the
pro-étale direct images are the unbounded right derived functors.

Writing $\mathrm{BC}_{\acute{e}t,K}$ and
$\mathrm{BC}_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t,\nu_X^*K}$ for the two base change
maps, one has

$$
\beta_K\circ\nu_{Y'}^*(\mathrm{BC}_{\acute{e}t,K})
=\mathrm{BC}_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t,\nu_X^*K}\circ\alpha_K.
$$

Thus these comparisons identify the pro-étale base change map with the
inverse image of the étale base change map. No torsion or finiteness
hypothesis on $\Lambda$ is needed.

Let $X$ be a scheme and $p$ a prime such that
$p=0$ in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. On $X_{\acute{e}t}$, put
$\varphi(a)=a^p$ and $K=\ker(\varphi-1:\mathbf G_a\to\mathbf G_a)$.
The sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow\mathbf G_a
\xrightarrow{\varphi-1}\mathbf G_a\longrightarrow0
$$

is short exact, and the map from the constant sheaf $\mathbf F_p$ to
$K$ is an isomorphism. Thus this is the Artin–Schreier sequence
$0\to\mathbf F_p\to\mathbf G_a\to\mathbf G_a\to0$.

$$
H^{q+1}(X_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf G_a)=0\qquad(q\geq0).
$$

group of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$.

Let

For a power series $f$, write $\rad(f)\in[0,\infty]$ for its radius

converge coefficientwise in the usual topology on $\mathbf C$ to $L$.
Then, for every $j\in J$,

$$
\rad(L)\le\rad(f_j).
$$

Independently, let $K$ be a complete nontrivially normed field and
$P\in K[t]$ with $P(0)\ne0$. Then

$$
|z|<\rad(P^{-1})\quad\Longrightarrow\quad P(z)\ne0
\qquad(z\in K),
$$

where $P^{-1}$ is the formal power series inverse of $P$.
In particular, if $f_j=P_j^{-1}$ for $P_j\in\mathbf C[t]$ with
$P_j(0)=1$, then $P_j$ has no zero on $|t|<\rad(L)$.

Finitely many $U$-admissible blow-ups of $T$ admit a common
$U$-admissible blow-up. A composite of two $U$-admissible blow-ups is

open $V\subseteq T$ containing $U$ extends to a $U$-admissible
blow-up of $T$.

$U$-admissible blow-up.

Let $T$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let $U\subseteq T$ be
an open. Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be a quasi-coherent ideal
of finite type with $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and write
$\pi:T_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)\to T$.
Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_{T_1}$ be a quasi-coherent ideal of
finite type equal to the unit ideal over $\pi^{-1}(U)$, and write
$q:T_2=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(T_1)\to T_1$.
There are a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ of
finite type, with $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and an isomorphism

$$
e:T_2\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(T)
$$

such that $b_{\mathcal K}\circ e=\pi\circ q$, where
$b_{\mathcal K}:\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(T)\to T$ is the blow-up morphism.
Thus the composite is again a blow-up with center disjoint from $U$;
the open $U$ need not be quasi-compact.

Let $T$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $V\subseteq T$ be a
quasi-compact open, and let $U\subseteq V$ be an open of $T$.
Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_V$ be a quasi-coherent ideal of finite
type with $\mathcal J|_U=\mathcal O_U$.
There are a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ of
finite type with $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal O_U$ and a morphism

$$
h:\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(V)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}(T)
$$

such that $b_{\mathcal K}\circ h=i\circ b_{\mathcal J}$, where
$i:V\hookrightarrow T$ is the inclusion and $b_{\mathcal K}$, $b_{\mathcal J}$ are the
blow-up morphisms, and the resulting square with bottom map $i$ is
cartesian. Thus the blow-up of $\mathcal K$ restricts over $V$ to the
given blow-up. The open $U$ need not be quasi-compact.

There is also a version without the containment $U\subseteq V$.
If $U,V\subseteq T$ are both quasi-compact opens and
$\mathcal J|_{U\cap V}=\mathcal O_{U\cap V}$, the same conclusion holds:
the extended center avoids all of $U$ and the square over $V$ is
cartesian.

objects.body:
Let $Z$ be a regular locally noetherian scheme over an algebraically
closed field $k$, and suppose that $Z$ is an étale limit, with affine
transition maps, of smooth surfaces over $k$. Let $D_1,D_2\subset Z$ be
regular divisors meeting transversely at exactly one point $z$; thus their
scheme-theoretic intersection is regular of codimension two in $Z$.
Choose a geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z$ over $z$
with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Write $S=Z_{(\bar z)}$, let $z_S$ be
its closed point, and put $D_{i,S}=D_i\times_Z S$.

Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$. For every $q\geq0$, the
restriction map

$$
H^q(S-D_{2,S},\mathbf F_\ell)\longrightarrow
H^q(D_{1,S}-z_S,\mathbf F_\ell)
$$

is bijective. Here the coefficients on the target are identified with
the pullback of the constant sheaf on the source.

invertible on $Y$, and let $q\geq1$. Suppose that $\mathrm{BC}(g,n,q-1)$ holds
and that $\mathrm{BC}(g,n,q)$ fails, that is, for some scheme $T$ over $Y$,
some qcqs morphism $Z\to T$ and some sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules on
$Z_{\acute{e}t}$, the base change map in degree $q$ along $Y'\times_YT\to T$ is not

an algebraically closed extension field $\Omega$ of $L$, an integer $m\geq1$
with $m\mid n$, and, for $C=Y'\times_YS$, the cartesian square

$$
\begin{CD}
C_\Omega @>{h}>> C\\
@VVV @VVV\\
\operatorname{Spec}\Omega @>>> S
\end{CD}
$$

such that

$$
R^qh_*\underline{\mathbf Z/m}\ne0.
$$

If $g$ is affine and smooth of relative dimension one, then $C$ is a smooth
affine curve over $S$.

attrs.title: Reduction to a unipotent local system

objects.body:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $U$ be a connected scheme, and let $G$ be a
finite locally constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces on
$U_{\acute{e}t}$. There are a connected scheme $V$, a finite étale
morphism $v:V\to U$, and a natural number $d$ prime to $\ell$ such that
every geometric fibre of $v$ has $d$ points and $v^*G$ has a finite
filtration

$$
0=W_0\hookrightarrow W_1\hookrightarrow
\cdots\hookrightarrow W_n\simeq v^*G
$$

whose successive cokernels are isomorphic to the constant sheaf
$\mathbf F_\ell$ on $V_{\acute{e}t}$. The length $n$ may be zero.

attrs.title: Reduction to a unipotent local system (1)

objects.body:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $U$ and $V$ be schemes with $V$ connected,
and let $G$ be a finite locally constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector
spaces on $U_{\acute{e}t}$. Let $v:V\to U$ be finite étale, and suppose
that every geometric fibre of $v$ has the same cardinality $d$, with
$\ell\nmid d$. The unit $\eta_G:G\to v_*v^*G$ has a retraction
$r:v_*v^*G\to G$:

$$
r\circ\eta_G=\id_G.
$$

In particular, $G$ is a direct summand of $v_*v^*G$.

Suppose that $f$ has a section $\sigma:S\to C$ and that

$$
\mathcal O_T\longrightarrow f_{T,*}\mathcal O_{C_T}
\quad\text{is an isomorphism for every }T\to S.
\tag{$\ast$}
$$

Then $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/S}(T)$ is identified, functorially in $T$,
with the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(\mathcal L,\alpha)$, with $\mathcal L$ invertible on
$C_T$ and $\alpha:\sigma_T^*\mathcal L\simeq\mathcal O_T$.
Every such pair has only the identity automorphism. There is a split
exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(T)
\xrightarrow{f_T^*}\operatorname{Pic}(C_T)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}_{C/S}(T)
\longrightarrow0,
$$

whose retraction is $\sigma_T^*$. The normalization map is

$$
\mathcal L\longmapsto
\mathcal L\otimes f_T^*(\sigma_T^*\mathcal L)^{-1}.
$$

Suppose that $f$ has a section $\sigma:S\to C$ and that

Then $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/S}(T)$ is identified, functorially in $T$,

Let $p:Z\to B$ be a morphism of schemes with a section $s:B\to Z$, and
suppose that

$$
\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)\longrightarrow\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)
$$

is surjective. Let $\mathcal A$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module,
let $\mathcal M$ be an $\mathcal O_Z$-module, and let
$\varphi,\psi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal M$ be morphisms with $\psi$ an
isomorphism. If $s^*\varphi=s^*\psi$, then $\varphi=\psi$.

In particular, under condition $(\ast)$, every automorphism of an
invertible sheaf on $C_T$ which preserves a trivialization along
$\sigma_T$ is the identity.

Let $f:C\to S$ have a section $\sigma:S\to C$, and suppose that
$\mathcal O_U\to f_{U,*}\mathcal O_{C_U}$ is an isomorphism for every
$U\to S$. Write $q_T:\operatorname{Pic}(C_T)\to\operatorname{Pic}_{C/S}(T)$
for the sheafification map. For every $T\to S$, the map

$$
\operatorname{Pic}(C_T)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Pic}(T)\times\operatorname{Pic}_{C/S}(T),
\qquad
[\mathcal L]\longmapsto
\bigl([\sigma_T^*\mathcal L],q_T([\mathcal L])\bigr)
$$

is bijective.
Together with $\sigma_T^*f_T^*=\mathrm{id}$ and the fact that two classes
have the same image under $q_T$ exactly when they differ by a class
pulled back from $T$, it gives the split exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(T)
\xrightarrow{f_T^*}\operatorname{Pic}(C_T)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}_{C/S}(T)
\longrightarrow0,
$$

whose retraction is $\sigma_T^*$.

Let $f:C\to S$ have a section $\sigma:S\to C$. For an invertible sheaf
$\mathcal L$ on $C_T$, its normalization is

$$
\mathcal L\longmapsto
\mathcal L\otimes f_T^*(\sigma_T^*\mathcal L)^{-1}.
$$

Its pullback along $\sigma_T$ is trivial. This construction needs no
condition $(\ast)$.

Normalized classes are determined by their twists in the following
sense. Let $\mathcal L,\mathcal L'$ be invertible sheaves on $C_T$ with
trivial pullback along $\sigma_T$. If an $\mathcal O_{C_T}$-module
$\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal O_T$-modules $\mathcal N,\mathcal N'$ admit
isomorphisms

$$
\mathcal L\simeq\mathcal P\otimes f_T^*\mathcal N,
\qquad
\mathcal L'\simeq\mathcal P\otimes f_T^*\mathcal N',
$$

then $[\mathcal L]=[\mathcal L']$ in $\operatorname{Pic}(C_T)$.
No invertibility assumption on $\mathcal P,\mathcal N,\mathcal N'$ and
no condition $(\ast)$ are required.

Let $i:U\to T$ be a quasi-compact immersion, with $T$ quasi-separated.
Its scheme-theoretic image $\overline U\subseteq T$ is a closed
subscheme, $U\to\overline U$ is an open immersion, and $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $\overline U$. The formation of
$\overline U$ commutes with flat base change $T'\to T$, in particular
with restriction to opens of $T$.

Let $i:U\to T$ be a quasi-compact morphism, and write
$U\xrightarrow{j}\overline U\xrightarrow{k}T$ for its factorization through
its scheme-theoretic image $\overline U$. Then

$$
\ker(\mathcal O_{\overline U}\to j_*\mathcal O_U)=0,
$$

so $j$ is scheme-theoretically dominant.

The morphism $k$ is a closed immersion by construction. If $i$ is
an immersion, $j$ is an open immersion, and hence identifies $U$
with a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme of $\overline U$. These
statements require no quasi-separatedness assumption on $T$.

The formation of
$\overline U$ commutes with flat base change $T'\to T$, in particular
with restriction to opens of $T$.

$V\setminus F_1$ and $V\setminus F_2$ are quasi-compact. There is a

\overline{b^{-1}(j(F_2))}=\varnothing,
$$

where the closures are taken in $T'$. Since $V$ is spectral, the
quasi-compactness of these complements is equivalent to the
constructibility of the closed subsets $F_i$.

Let $S$ be integral and let $f:X\to S$ be separated, smooth and of finite type. For a finite locally constant
$\Fell$-sheaf $L$ on $X_{\acute{e}t}$, there is a nonempty open
$S_0\subset S$ with the following property. For the restriction
$f_{S_0}:X_{S_0}\to S_0$, the complex $Rf_{S_0,*}L$ is bounded with
finite locally constant cohomology sheaves, and its formation commutes
with base change. Namely, for every $k$-scheme $v:T\to S_0$ of finite type, with
base change $f_T:X_T\to T$ and $v_X:X_T\to X_{S_0}$, the canonical
base change map $v^*Rf_{S_0,*}L\to Rf_{T,*}v_X^*L$ is an isomorphism.

Weakly étale morphisms are stable under base change and composition,
and the property is local on source and target for the Zariski topology.
Every $X$-morphism between two weakly étale $X$-schemes is weakly
étale. Ind-étale ring maps are stable under base change and
composition. On affine charts, a morphism
$\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is weakly étale if and
only if both

$$
R\longrightarrow B,
\qquad B\otimes_RB\longrightarrow B
$$

are flat.

Let $f:U\to X$ be weakly étale and let $X'\to X$ be any morphism
of schemes. Then $U\times_XX'\to X'$ is weakly étale.

Let $V\to U$ and $U\to X$ be weakly étale morphisms of schemes.
Then their composite $V\to X$ is weakly étale.

Let $f:U\to X$ be a morphism of schemes and let $U=\bigcup_iU_i$
be a Zariski open covering. Then $f$ is weakly étale if and only if
every restriction $U_i\to X$ is weakly étale.

Let $f:U\to X$ be a morphism of schemes and let $X=\bigcup_iX_i$
be a Zariski open covering. Then $f$ is weakly étale if and only if
every restriction $f^{-1}(X_i)\to X_i$ is weakly étale.

Let $u:U\to X$ and $v:V\to X$ be weakly étale morphisms of
schemes. If $h:U\to V$ satisfies $v\circ h=u$, then $h$ is weakly
étale.

Let $R\to B$ be an ind-étale map of commutative rings and let
$R\to R'$ be any ring map. Then $R'\to R'\otimes_RB$ is ind-étale.
Equivalently, in any pushout square of commutative rings, the base
change of an ind-étale map is ind-étale.

Let $R\to B$ and $B\to C$ be ind-étale maps of commutative rings.
Then their composite $R\to C$ is ind-étale.

A morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is weakly
étale if and only if both

$$
R\longrightarrow B,
\qquad B\otimes_RB\longrightarrow B
$$

are flat.
*Shared context.* Use the notions of weakly etale morphism and ind-etale ring map already defined.

piece of $\bigwedge^rV$ displayed above is nonzero.

Let $P$ be a proper geometrically integral $k$-scheme, let $T$ be a
$k$-scheme of finite type, let $f:P\times T\to T$ be the projection,
and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible sheaf on $P\times T$. For $t\in T$
write $P_t=P\times_k\kappa(t)$ and $\mathcal L_t=\mathcal L|_{P_t}$.

1. $\mathcal L_t$ is trivial if and only if $H^0(P_t,\mathcal L_t)\ne0$
   and $H^0(P_t,\mathcal L_t^{-1})\ne0$.
2. The set of $t\in T$ such that $\mathcal L_t$ is trivial is closed.

Let $f:X\to T$ be proper with geometrically integral fibres, and let
$\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be invertible sheaves on $X$ with an
isomorphism $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B\simeq\mathcal O_X$.
For every $t\in T$,

$$
\mathcal A_t\simeq\mathcal O_{X_t}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
h^0(X_t,\mathcal A_t)>0\ \text{and}\ h^0(X_t,\mathcal B_t)>0.
$$

Taking $X=P\times_k T$, $\mathcal A=\mathcal L$ and
$\mathcal B=\mathcal L^{-1}$, this says that $\mathcal L_t$ is trivial if and only if
$H^0(P_t,\mathcal L_t)\ne0$ and $H^0(P_t,\mathcal L_t^{-1})\ne0$.

Let $f:X\to T$ be proper, flat and locally of finite presentation,
with geometrically integral fibres, and let $\mathcal M$ and
$\mathcal N$ be invertible sheaves on $X$. Then

$$
\{t\in T\mid\mathcal M_t\simeq\mathcal N_t\}
$$

is closed in $T$. Taking $X=P\times_k T$, $\mathcal M=\mathcal L$
and $\mathcal N=\mathcal O_X$, the set of $t\in T$ such that $\mathcal L_t$ is trivial is closed.

Let $P$ be a proper geometrically integral $k$-scheme, let $T$ be a
$k$-scheme of finite type, let $f:P\times T\to T$ be the projection,

write $P_t=P\times_k\kappa(t)$ and $\mathcal L_t=\mathcal L|_{P_t}$.

The clauses below are stated more generally, for a proper morphism $f:X\to T$ with
geometrically integral fibres. There we write $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$,
$\mathcal F_t=\mathcal F|_{X_t}$ and
$h^0(X_t,\mathcal F_t)=\dim_{\kappa(t)}H^0(X_t,\mathcal F_t)$.
For closedness we also require $f$ to be flat and locally of finite
presentation. These hypotheses hold for the projection $P\times_k T\to T$,
even without the finite type assumption on $T$.

Let $P$ and $Q$ be proper geometrically integral $k$-schemes with points
$p_0\in P(k)$ and $q_0\in Q(k)$, let $T$ be a $k$-scheme of finite type,
and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible sheaf on $P\times Q\times T$ whose
restrictions to $p_0\times Q\times T$ and to $P\times q_0\times T$ are
trivial. If $\mathcal L$ is trivial on the fibre over a point $t\in T$,
then $\mathcal L$ is trivial on $P\times Q\times U$ for an open
neighbourhood $U$ of $t$.

Let $P$ and $Q$ be proper geometrically integral $k$-schemes with points
$p_0\in P(k)$ and $q_0\in Q(k)$, let $T$ be a $k$-scheme,
and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible sheaf on $P\times Q\times T$ whose
restrictions to $p_0\times Q\times T$ and to $P\times q_0\times T$ are
trivial. Write $f:P\times Q\times T\to T$ for the projection. If
$\mathcal L_t\simeq\mathcal O_{P\times Q\times\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}$
for a point $t\in T$, then there are an open neighbourhood $U$ of $t$
and a section

$$
\sigma\in H^0(f^{-1}(U),\mathcal L)
$$

which freely generates $\mathcal L|_{f^{-1}(U)}$. Thus multiplication
by $\sigma$ gives an isomorphism
$\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(U)}\simeq\mathcal L|_{f^{-1}(U)}$.

and such that for every $k$-scheme $T'\to U'$ of finite type the base
change map for $j'$ along $T'$ is an isomorphism. Then there is a nonempty

Let $M$ be an irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on a dense open
$U_0\subset\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$. If $M$ is unramified at infinity and is not geometrically constant,
then no geometric constituent of $M$ is of the form
$\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}$ with $a\in\bar k_0$.

Let $k_0$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $\ell\ne p$ be
prime, and let $M$ be a lisse Weil $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf on a
dense open $U_0\subset\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$. Put
$U=U_0\otimes_{k_0}\bar k_0$, and let
$\psi:k_0\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$ be an additive character.

1. If $M$ is irreducible and $\mathcal L_{\psi(0x)}|_U$ is a geometric
   constituent of $M$, then $M$ is geometrically constant. This assertion
   does not require $\psi$ to be nontrivial or $M$ to be unramified at infinity.
2. If $\psi$ is nontrivial and $M$ is unramified at infinity, then no
   geometric constituent of $M$ is $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$ for
   $a\in\bar k_0^\times$. This assertion does not require $M$ to be irreducible.

Here a geometric constituent is a quotient of a lisse subsheaf of $M|_U$.
Unramifiedness at infinity means that $M$ extends to a lisse Weil sheaf on
$U_0\cup\{\infty\}\subset\mathbf P^1_{k_0}$, and geometric constancy means
that $M|_U$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

In particular, if $\psi$ is nontrivial and $M$ is irreducible, unramified
at infinity and not geometrically constant, then no geometric constituent
of $M$ is of the form $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$ with $a\in\bar k_0$.

fixed point of $\Phi_X^m$, and suppose $K_{\bar y}=0$. Then

$$
\rho:R\Gamma_\Gamma(T,P)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_y(\Delta,\delta^*P)
$$

is zero in $D(A)$. Consequently $\operatorname{LT}_y(\psi)=0$ for every

attrs.title: Vanishing of the local term at a zero stalk

objects.body:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X/k$ be a separated, quasi-compact
smooth curve, and let $h:X\to X$ be a $k$-endomorphism fixing $y\in X(k)$
such that $h^\#\mathfrak m_y\subseteq\mathfrak m_y^2$. Let $\ell$ be a
prime invertible in $k$, let $A$ be a finite commutative $\ell$-primary
ring, and let $L,K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,A)$ with $K_{\bar y}=0$.
On the strict localization $T$ of $X\times_k X$ at $(y,y)$, let
$\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be the inverse images of the transposed graph
$(h,\operatorname{id}_X)$ and the diagonal, and put
$P=(L\boxtimes K)|_T$. Then the supported restriction

$$
\rho:R\Gamma_\Gamma(T,P)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_y(\Delta,\delta^*P)
$$

is zero in $D(A)$. In particular, this applies to $h=\Phi_X^m$, $m\geq1$,
and $L=\mathbb D_XK$ in Lemma [lemma-local-term-restriction-map].

There is also a $\Qbarl$-coefficient form. Let $k$ be an algebraically
closed extension of a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic different
from $\ell$, and let $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ be a separated smooth curve,
with $X_0$ of finite type over $k_0$. Let $m\geq1$ and
$K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Qbarl)$. Use the graph convention $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi_X^m)$, put
$P'=K\boxtimes\mathbb D_XK$, and write $F=\Fix(c)$, with maps
$\iota:F\to X$ to the source of the graph and $d:F\to X$ to the
diagonal. If $z:\operatorname{Spec}k\to F$ has image $y\in X(k)$ and
$K_{\bar y}=0$, then the pullback along $z$ of

$$
\rho_{P'}:L\iota^*Rc^!P'\longrightarrow Rd^!L\delta^*P'
$$

is zero. Interchanging the two factors of $X\times_k X$ identifies
this convention with the transposed graph and
$\mathbb D_XK\boxtimes K$ of Lemma [lemma-local-term-restriction-map].

Consequently $\operatorname{LT}_y(\psi)=0$ for every
morphism $\psi:(\Phi_X^m)^*K\to K$.

attrs.title: Vanishing of the local term at a zero stalk (2)

objects.body:
Let $T$ be the strict localization of a smooth surface at a closed
point $t$. Let $H$ be a regular curve through $t$, and let $D$ and $C$ be reduced
closed curves through $t$ such that the tangent cone of $D$ at $t$ meets
the tangent cones of $C$ and of $H$ only in $0$.
Let $j':T-(D\cup H)\hookrightarrow T-D$ be the open immersion and let $N$ be a bounded
complex on $T-(D\cup H)$ with finite locally constant cohomology and
finite $\ell$-group monodromy. Then the restriction map

$$
R\Gamma(T-D,j'_!N)\longrightarrow
R\Gamma(C-t,(j'_!N)|_{C-t})
$$

is zero in $D(A)$.

attrs.title: Vanishing of restrictions after blowing up

objects.body:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible
in $k$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring. Let
$T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be the strict localization of a smooth surface
over $k$ at a closed point $t$, and let $\m$ be the maximal ideal of $R$.
Choose $f,g,h\in R$ with

$$
f\ne0,\qquad 0\ne g\in\m,\qquad h\in\m-\m^2.
$$

Put $D=V(f)$, $C=V(g)$ and $H=V(h)$. Suppose that the tangent cone
of $D$ meets those of $C$ and $H$ only in $0$. Let
$j':T-(D\cup H)\hookrightarrow T-D$ be the open immersion, and let $N$
be a bounded complex of étale $A$-modules on $T-(D\cup H)$. Assume
that each cohomology sheaf of $N$ becomes constant with finite fibre
on a finite étale Galois cover whose group is a finite $\ell$-group.
Then the restriction map

$$
R\Gamma(T-D,j'_!N)\longrightarrow
R\Gamma(C-t,(j'_!N)|_{C-t})
$$

is zero in $D(A)$.

attrs.title: Vanishing of restrictions in principal equations

objects.body:

Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}(D)$ be an object of $X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$ with $D$
w-contractible. Then every epimorphism of sheaves $F\to h_U$ has a
section. Equivalently, $h_U$ is projective in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t})$.
More generally, for an object $W$ of $X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$ the following are
equivalent: every epimorphism of sheaves of sets $F\to h_W$ admits a
section; $h_W$ is projective in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t})$; every epimorphism
$F\to G$ induces a surjection $F(W)\to G(W)$.

attrs.title: Sections of epimorphisms onto w-contractible affines

objects.body:
Let $U$ be an object of $X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$ whose underlying scheme is
isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(D)$, with $D$ w-contractible. For sheaves of
sets $F,G$ in any fixed universe, every locally surjective morphism
$\varphi:F\to G$ induces a surjection

$$
F(U)\longrightarrow G(U).
$$

attrs.title: Surjectivity on sections over w-contractible affines

objects.body:
For an object $W$ of $X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$ the following are equivalent: every
epimorphism of sheaves of sets $F\to h_W$ admits a section; $h_W$ is
projective in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t})$; every epimorphism $F\to G$ induces a
surjection $F(W)\to G(W)$.

Let $X_0$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k_0$, let $F$ be a
constructible Weil sheaf on $X_0$, let $k_m\supset k_0$ be the
extension of degree $m$, and let $u\in\mathbf R$. The group
$H^r_c(X,F)$ is the same for $X_0$ and for $X_0\otimes_{k_0}k_m$, and
the geometric Frobenius of $k_m$ acts on it as the $m$th power of that
of $k_0$. Every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of the Frobenius of $k_0$ on
$H^r_c(X,F)$ satisfies $|\iota\alpha|\le q^{u/2}$ if and only if every
eigenvalue $\beta$ of the Frobenius of $k_m$ satisfies
$|\iota\beta|\le q^{mu/2}$.

Let $f:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated of finite type, and let $K$ be a
constructible Weil sheaf on $X_0$, mixed of weights at most $w$.

1. Let $j:U_0\to X_0$ be an open immersion with closed complement
   $i:Z_0\to X_0$. If $R^q(fj)_!j^*K$ and $R^q(fi)_!i^*K$ are mixed of

   of weights at most $w+q$ for every $q$, then so is $R^qf_!K$.

attrs.title: Weights via the kernel and coimage

objects.body:
Every constructible Weil $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is
mixed. A constructible Weil $E$-sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$
becomes mixed after extending scalars to a finite extension of $E$

attrs.title: Weil sheaves on a point are mixed

objects.body:
Let $k_0=\Fq$, let $\ell\nmid q$ be prime, and fix an embedding

separated quasi-finite $k_0$-scheme. Every constructible Weil
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $X_0$ is $\iota$-mixed.
In particular, this holds for $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$.

sheaf of the third term is an extension of a kernel by a cokernel of maps
between cohomology sheaves of the other two. Since $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$
is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions
(Proposition [proposition-ind-constructible-sheaves]), the third term lies in
$\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ whenever the other two do. Closure under shifts is

subcategory of $D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$ containing $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$. It
therefore contains the smallest one, $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$.

triangulated subcategory, and for extensions we use the vanishing of

comparing cohomology sheaves.

For kernels and cokernels the first assertion follows from exactness and
full faithfulness of $\nu_X^*$. Indeed, a map between classical sheaves is
$\nu_X^*$ of a map of étale sheaves, and $\nu_X^*$ carries its kernel
and cokernel to the kernel and cokernel. Given an extension
$0\to\nu_X^*F\to G\to\nu_X^*F'\to0$, we apply $\nu_{X,*}$. Since
$R^1\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*F=0$ by Theorem [theorem-bounded-below-cohomology-comparison], the
result $0\to F\to\nu_{X,*}G\to F'\to0$ is exact, and the counit maps
its pullback to the original extension. This map is the identity on the
outer terms, so by the five lemma $G\simeq\nu_X^*\nu_{X,*}G$ is classical.

The functor $\nu_X^*$ lands in classical complexes and is fully

cohomology sheaves. This reduces
the claim to a single shifted constructible sheaf, and for it the filtration
from Lemma [lemma-constructible-sheaves](3) yields finitely many short
exact sequences, that is, distinguished triangles, with terms $a_!L$.

Take $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega)$ in the theorem and apply the
functor of global sections on $Y'_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$. By
Proposition [proposition-pro-etale-site-separably-closed] the topos of $Y'_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$ is that
of condensed sets, where global sections is evaluation at the point.
This functor is exact, because every surjection of profinite sets onto
a point has a section. On the right we therefore get the cohomology of
the fibre. On the left, $(Rf_*K)_{\bar y}$ means
$\Gamma(Y'_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\bar y^*Rf_*K)$, and by the proof of the theorem we have
$Rf_*K\simeq\nu_Y^*Rf_*K_{\acute{e}t}$. Since

the constant condensed complex on the étale stalk
$(Rf_*K_{\acute{e}t})_{\bar y}$, so its global sections are that stalk. Finally, by
the theorem on the étale site, this stalk is the étale cohomology of the fibre.

We translate irreducibility into the surjectivity of $\pi_1(C)$ onto
one finite group, and then find $C$ with Bertini's theorem applied to
the corresponding cover.

Choose a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ over which all the sheaves are
defined, and apply Lemma [lemma-detecting-irreducibility-finite-quotient] to their geometric
representations. Let $T\to X$ be the connected Galois cover
corresponding to the intersection of the kernels of the resulting
finite quotients of $\pi_1(X)$, and let $Q$ be its group. In dimension
one, we take $C=X$. Otherwise $\dim X\ge2$, and we apply
Lemma [lemma-curve-preserving-finite-cover] to $T$ and the given
points. If no points are given we add one, since the lemma needs $S$
nonempty. As $T\times_XC$ is connected, $\pi_1(C)$ acts transitively on
the fibre of the $Q$-torsor $T\times_XC\to C$, so its image in $Q$ is
all of $Q$. Each of the finite quotients above is a quotient of $Q$.
Hence $\pi_1(C)$ has the same image as $\pi_1(X)$ in each of them, and
Lemma [lemma-detecting-irreducibility-finite-quotient], applied with $\Pi=\pi_1(X)$ and
$\Pi'$ the image of $\pi_1(C)$, shows that the restrictions remain
geometrically irreducible. By
Lemma [lemma-curve-preserving-finite-cover] the curve and the points
are defined over a finite extension of the constant field. The curve
$C$ is geometrically connected because it is connected over
$\overline{\mathbf F}_q$.
This clause is proved by the proof of Corollary [corollary-curve-preserving-geometric-irreducibility], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

the map $d\mapsto\mathcal O_C(dP)$ is a section of the degree, which is
therefore surjective.

over a field this loses nothing, because linear duality is exact.
