The first assertion is the refinement theorem applied chart by chart, and
the second is then formal.

Given an object $U$ of $X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$, cover $X$ by affine opens and cover their inverse images in $U$ by
affine opens. These Zariski coverings are pro-étale coverings, so it
suffices to cover each chart. On such a chart the map is a weakly
étale ring map $R\to B$.
By Theorem [theorem-pro-etale-refinements-weakly-etale] there is a single faithfully flat
cover $\operatorname{Spec}(B')\to\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ such that
$\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is a limit of
affine schemes étale over $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, hence over
$X$. The equivalence of categories of sheaves follows from the comparison
lemma for sites; see [bhatt-scholze15, Lemma 4.2.4].

Cover $X$ by affine opens and their inverse images in $U$ by affine opens. These are pro-étale coverings, so it suffices to treat a chart corresponding to a weakly étale map $R\to B$. Theorem [theorem-pro-etale-refinements-weakly-etale] provides a faithfully flat cover $\operatorname{Spec}(B')\to\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ with $B'$ ind-étale over $R$. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is a pro-étale affine over $X$. Composing the coverings proves the assertion.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-pro-etale-affines-form-basis].

By clause [proposition-pro-etale-affines-form-basis--1], the full subsite of pro-étale affines covers every object of $X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$. The induced topology is the restriction of the original topology. The comparison lemma for sites therefore makes restriction an equivalence on sheaves; it applies both to sets and, by preserving the abelian group operations, to abelian sheaves. This is the comparison used in [bhatt-scholze15, Lemma 4.2.4].

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-pro-etale-affines-form-basis].

Part (1) is the covering condition of Definition [definition-small-pro-etale-site] with
$W=U$. For (2), recall that flat morphisms locally of finite presentation
are open. By quasi-compactness we then find the required finite refinements; see
[Stacks, [098B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/098B)].

Apply the covering condition of Definition [definition-small-pro-etale-site] with $W=U$. It gives finitely many affine pieces whose images cover $U$. Their finite disjoint union is affine, and its map to $U$ is flat and surjective, hence faithfully flat.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-pro-etale-coverings–1].

An étale morphism is weakly étale and is open, since it is flat and locally of finite presentation. On a quasi-compact affine test object, finitely many affine pieces of an étale covering therefore cover. This verifies the covering condition; Zariski coverings are a special case. See [Stacks, [098B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/098B)].

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-pro-etale-coverings–1].

Since a finitely presented étale $\Omega$-algebra is a finite product of
copies of $\Omega$, filtered colimits of such algebras correspond,
under $\operatorname{Spec}$, to inverse limits of finite sets. Under this correspondence, faithfully
flat covering maps become surjections of profinite sets, and by
quasi-compactness every cover can be refined by a finite one, so the
sites are equivalent. The topoi then agree because the pro-étale affines
form a basis and sheaves are determined by their values on them. Finally, the
last assertion is the definition of the condensed ring
$\underline R$ of a topological ring $R$ given above, whose sections over a
profinite set $S$ are the continuous maps $S\to R$; for discrete $R$
these are the locally constant functions, which are the sections of
the classical constant sheaf.

A finitely presented étale $\Omega$-algebra is a finite product of copies of the separably closed field $\Omega$. Filtered colimits of these algebras correspond under $\operatorname{Spec}$ to inverse limits of finite sets. Faithfully flat covers correspond to jointly surjective families of profinite sets, and quasi-compactness refines these to finite families. This identifies both the categories and their covering families.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-pro-etale-site-separably-closed].

Pro-étale affines form a basis, so sheaves on the full site are determined by this basis. Clause [proposition-pro-etale-site-separably-closed--1] identifies the basis and its topology with the profinite site defining condensed sets, using the same set-theoretic cutoff. Their categories of sheaves are therefore equivalent.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-pro-etale-site-separably-closed].

The condensed ring $\underline R$ has as sections on a profinite $S$ the continuous maps $S\to R$. For discrete $A$, these are locally constant functions, exactly the sections of the classical constant sheaf. For a profinite or locally profinite ring the same definition gives the asserted continuous-function sheaf.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-pro-etale-site-separably-closed].

Both claims are first checked on $\Dbc$ and then extended. Tensor
products and both sides of the projection map commute with direct sums
and cones in each variable. Hence, fixing all variables but one, the

(Lemma [lemma-checking-isomorphisms-constructible-complexes]). By the
dévissage of Corollary [corollary-coefficient-heart-b], $\Dbc$ is closed
under $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$, since $a_!L\otimes^{\mathbf L}b_!M$ is the
extension by zero of a lisse sheaf on the intersection of the two strata. The projection formula on $\Dbc$ is
Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-constructible-complexes].

On $\Dbc$, use Corollary [corollary-coefficient-heart-b]: tensor products reduce to $a_!L\otimes^{\mathbf L}b_!M$, which is extension by zero of a lisse sheaf on the intersection of the strata. Thus the constructible generators are closed under tensor. Tensor is exact and preserves direct sums in either variable. Apply the localizing-subcategory criterion of Lemma [lemma-checking-isomorphisms-constructible-complexes] successively to the two variables to obtain closure of the whole localizing category.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-projection-formula-rational-coefficients].

For constructible $M,N$, the comparison is an isomorphism by Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-constructible-complexes]. Proper direct image preserves direct sums by Lemma [lemma-proper-direct-image-unbounded-complexes--3], and tensor and pullback preserve direct sums and cones. For fixed constructible $M$, the objects $N$ for which the map is an isomorphism therefore form the whole localizing category. Keeping such $N$ fixed and repeating in $M$ proves the assertion for both variables.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-projection-formula-rational-coefficients].

Theorem [theorem-proper-base-change-classical-pro] applies at each
finite level, so the point is that $Rp_*$ and the completed inverse
images are compatible with the passage to the derived limit of the
reductions.

The reductions of $Rp_*K$ are controlled by the projection formula. The
projection formula map (4.14) for
$M=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_Y$ is a map

$$
(Rp_*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_Y
\longrightarrow Rp_*K_n,
$$

which we regard in $D(Y_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)$. We claim that it is an
isomorphism. Since restriction of scalars to $\mathcal O_E$ is conservative,
we may check this after forgetting the $\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$-structure.
Now the ring $\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$ has the free resolution
$[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_E]$, so by
Corollary [corollary-finite-quotients-their-transition-maps] the source is the cone of
$\pi_E^n$ on $Rp_*K$, and the target is $Rp_*$ of the cone of $\pi_E^n$ on
$K$. These agree because $Rp_*$ is triangulated and $\mathcal O_E$-linear.
Moreover, the resolutions for $n+1$ and $n$ are related by the chain map
$(\pi_E,\mathrm{id})$, and applying $Rp_*$ to it shows that these
comparisons form an isomorphism of towers. Since all these constructions can
be made on complexes with functorial resolutions, the comparisons
define a map in the derived category of towers of
Definition [definition-derived-adic-completeness].

Since $K$ is derived complete, it is the derived
limit of its reductions $K_n$, and since the functor $Rp_*$ is a right adjoint, it
commutes with derived limits, and we obtain

$$
Rp_*K\simeq Rp_*R\varprojlim_nK_n
\simeq R\varprojlim_nRp_*K_n.
$$

By the reduction comparisons, the right side is the derived limit of the
reductions $(Rp_*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_Y$, that is,
the derived completion of $Rp_*K$. Hence the completion map of $Rp_*K$ is an
isomorphism, and $Rp_*K$ is derived complete. The definition of completed
inverse image and the same right-adjoint property for $Rp'_*$ now give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hat g^*Rp_*K
&\simeq R\varprojlim_n g^*Rp_*K_n,\\
Rp'_*\hat g'^*K
&\simeq R\varprojlim_n Rp'_*g'^*K_n.
\end{aligned}
$$

The base change maps $g^*Rp_*K_n\to Rp'_*g'^*K_n$ are natural in $K_n$, so
they form a map of towers, and each is an isomorphism by
Theorem [theorem-proper-base-change-classical-pro]. Its cone therefore has zero cohomology
at every level, and applying $R\varprojlim$ gives the asserted
isomorphism.

We show that both stalks are the sections over the same geometric fibre.
To this end, choose $\bar y':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$ and use the
composite $\bar y=g\bar y'$ as the geometric point of $Y$. Since properness
is preserved by base change, Lemma [lemma-sections-geometric-fibre]
applies to $f'$ as well as to $f$. Moreover, the cartesian square identifies

$$
X'_{\bar y'}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=X_{\bar y}
$$

and identifies the two inverse image sheaves on it. Thus the stalks of
both sides of the desired map are the same set of sections. It remains to see that the map is the identity. The underived
base change map sends a section
represented over $X\times_YV$ to its
restriction to the base change of the neighbourhood, and hence to its
restriction to this same fibre. In other words, the map on stalks is the
identity under the displayed identifications. Since geometric stalks detect
isomorphisms, this proves the assertion.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-proper-base-change-degree-zero], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper. We first reduce to the case that $Y$ is affine,
as Chow's lemma requires. Let $Y=\bigcup U$ be an affine open cover, and
assume $\mathrm{PBC}_\Lambda$ for each restriction $f^{-1}(U)\to U$. Given a base change
$Y'\to Y$, the inverse images $U'$ of the sets $U$ then cover $Y'$. Since higher
direct images commute with restriction to open subschemes, the restriction
of the base change map to $U'$ is the base change map of $f^{-1}(U)\to U$
along $U'\to U$, hence an isomorphism. As isomorphisms can be checked on
geometric stalks, the base change map over $Y'$ is an isomorphism.

Now $Y$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so
Theorem [theorem-chow-s-lemma-projective-form] with $S=Y$ gives a proper surjection
$\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ and closed immersions
$i_Y:\widetilde X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$ and
$i_X=(\pi,i_Y):\widetilde X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_X$ with $f\pi$ equal to
$i_Y$ followed by the projection. Here we need Chow's lemma over a base
that is affine but need not be Noetherian; we prove this form
in Appendix [chap-Nagata-compactification-and-Chows-lemma]. The two maps $\pi$ and $f\pi$ factor as
closed immersions $i_X$ and $i_Y$ followed by projections of projective
spaces. Closed immersions are finite, so they satisfy $\mathrm{PBC}_\Lambda$ by
Lemma [lemma-finite-morphisms], and projections of projective spaces satisfy
$\mathrm{PBC}_\Lambda$ by the hypothesis and
Lemma [lemma-pbc-projective-space]. By stability under
composition (Lemma [lemma-composition-cancellation](i)), both $\pi$ and
$f\pi$ therefore satisfy $\mathrm{PBC}_\Lambda$. As $\pi$ is surjective, we may cancel it by
Lemma [lemma-composition-cancellation](ii), and this gives
$\mathrm{PBC}_\Lambda$ for $f$.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-proper-base-change-etale-site], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

On $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$ the base change map is an isomorphism by
Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-constructible-complexes], so by Lemma [lemma-checking-isomorphisms-constructible-complexes] it suffices
to show that $g^*Rp_*$ and $Rp'_*g'^*$ are exact functors
$\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y',\Lambda))$ preserving direct sums.
For $Rp_*$ and $Rp'_*$ this is Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-extension-zero], so it remains to treat inverse image. It is exact and preserves direct sums, and it sends $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(-,\Lambda)$ into
$D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(-,\Lambda)$. Indeed, for finite $A$ this holds because of bounded flat constructible representatives, and for $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ it holds because pullback preserves the local description of constructible
sheaves on strata (Lemma [lemma-inverse-image-tensor-product] in the integral case). Given this, the localizing-subcategory argument before Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-extension-zero] shows that inverse image also preserves $\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(-,\Lambda))$.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-proper-base-change-localizing-categories], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

For a torsion sheaf we compare the two sides on geometric stalks. Both
stalks are the cohomology of a projective line over a separably closed
field, and the base change map becomes the pullback along a field
extension. Bounded below complexes then follow by truncation.

Let $F$ be a torsion sheaf. Choose a geometric
point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ and put
$\bar s=g\bar t$. Then the strict localizations fit into a natural map
$T_{(\bar t)}\to S_{(\bar s)}$ of strictly henselian local schemes.
Write $k_s,k_t$ for their residue fields; these are separably closed,
and the map induces an inclusion $k_s\hookrightarrow k_t$.
For each $q\geq0$, using (4.12) and
Proposition [proposition-cohomology-p-1-over-henselian], we obtain the commutative diagram

$$
\begin{CD}
(g^*R^q\pi_*F)_{\bar t}
@>>>
(R^q\pi'_*g'^*F)_{\bar t}\\
@V{\sim}VV @VV{\sim}V\\
H^q(\mathbf P^1_{S_{(\bar s)}},F|)
@>>> H^q(\mathbf P^1_{T_{(\bar t)}},F|)\\
@V{\sim}VV @VV{\sim}V\\
H^q(\mathbf P^1_{k_s},F|)
@>>> H^q(\mathbf P^1_{k_t},F|).
\end{CD}
$$

Here the top arrow is the stalk at $\bar t$ of
the map induced by
(4.3) on $q$th cohomology sheaves, while the middle and
bottom arrows are the natural pullback maps. The
top square commutes by the definition of the base change map: a section over
$\mathbf P^1_V$, for a pointed étale neighbourhood $V\to S$, is pulled
back to $\mathbf P^1_{V\times_ST}$, and passing to the limits over the two strict
localizations gives exactly the middle arrow. The bottom square commutes
by naturality of restriction to the closed fibres.

The vertical arrows are isomorphisms: the upper ones by
(4.12), applied to $\pi$ and to $\pi'$; here
$\mathbf P^1_{S_{(\bar s)}}$ and $\mathbf P^1_{T_{(\bar t)}}$ are the base
changes of $\mathbf P^1_S$ and $\mathbf P^1_T$ to the strict
localizations. The lower ones are isomorphisms by Proposition [proposition-cohomology-p-1-over-henselian],
applied to the strictly henselian local rings of $S_{(\bar s)}$ and
$T_{(\bar t)}$. Hence the top arrow is an isomorphism as soon as the bottom
arrow is, and the bottom arrow is an isomorphism by
Lemma [lemma-extension-separably-closed-ground-field], applied to $C=\mathbf P^1_{k_s}$ and
the extension $k_s\subseteq k_t$. Thus every geometric stalk
of $g^*R^q\pi_*F\to R^q\pi'_*g'^*F$ is an isomorphism.
As geometric stalks are conservative, the base change map for $F$ is an
isomorphism in $D^+(T_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf Z)$. Moreover, cohomology and higher direct images
of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules agree with those of their underlying abelian
sheaves (Lemma [lemma-cohomology-modules-underlying-abelian]).
Hence the base change map for $F$ is also an isomorphism in $D^+(T_{\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$.

Now let
$K\in D^+(\mathbf P^1_{S,\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$ have torsion cohomology and
fix $m\in\mathbf Z$. The two functors
$g^*R\pi_*,\ R\pi'_*g'^*:D^+(\mathbf P^1_{S,\acute{e}t},\Lambda)\to
D^+(T_{\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$ send $D^{\geq m+1}$ into $D^{\geq m+1}$, since inverse image is exact and derived direct image is
left $t$-exact. Using the truncation triangle for $\tau_{\leq m}K$,
we can therefore reduce the assertion in degree $m$ to the bounded complex $\tau_{\leq m}K$.
By induction on the length, using the truncation triangles and
naturality of the base change map, we reduce further to the
shifted torsion sheaves $H^a(K)[-a]$. For these the assertion has already been proved.

For $\mathrm{IA}_\Lambda(\pi)$, let $I$ be a torsion injective sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules. Then $R^q\pi_*I=0$ for $q>0$, and the case of sheaves gives
$R^q\pi'_*g'^*I\simeq g^*R^q\pi_*I=0$.

*Finite coefficients.* Part (1), including the Tor bound, is
Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-finite-coefficients], and proper base change holds by
Theorem [theorem-proper-base-change-classical-pro] with $\Lambda=A$.
The projection formula, finally, is the classical torsion
formula [Stacks, [0F0G](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0G)] in $D(Y_{\acute{e}t},A)$, transported to
$D(Y_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},A)$ by pullback from the étale site.

*Integral coefficients.* Let $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. We first show that $Rp_*K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, by computing its reduction as in (4.15) below. By
Proposition [proposition-integral-constructibility-criterion] and
Lemma [lemma-bounds-finite-reductions], $K$ is derived complete with
bounded classical finite reductions. Hence
Proposition [proposition-proper-base-change-complete-integral] applies. It
shows that $Rp_*K$ is derived complete and gives a canonical comparison
of reductions

$$
\rho_K:(Rp_*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_{E,Y}/\pi_E
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } Rp_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_{E,X}/\pi_E).
\tag{4.15}
$$

The target of $\rho_K$ is constructible and
bounded. Indeed, it is the direct image of a torsion complex pulled back
from $X_{\acute{e}t}$ [Stacks, [09B1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09B1)], so it is the pullback to $Y_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$ of the
direct image in $D(Y_{\acute{e}t},\mathbf F_E)$ [Stacks, [09A6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09A6)]. The latter is
constructible by the finiteness theorem for proper direct image
with torsion coefficients [Stacks, [0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0)], and bounded because $p$ has
finite cohomological dimension [Stacks, [0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10)]. Now
Proposition [proposition-integral-constructibility-criterion] gives
$Rp_*K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$.

Proper base change holds by
Lemma [lemma-completed-ordinary-base-change], which applies
because $g^*Rp_*K$ and $g'^*K$ are derived complete, as inverse image
preserves integral constructibility (Lemma [lemma-integral-models](3)).

The projection formula is tested modulo $\pi_E$ in the same way. Let $C$ be
the cone of the projection formula map for $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and
$M\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. Its source $Rp_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}M$ and
target $Rp_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*M)$ are integrally constructible, by
Lemma [lemma-integral-models](3) and the fact just proved that $Rp_*$
maps $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. As objects of
$\Dbc$ they are derived complete, and hence so is $C$. Derived
Nakayama (Lemma [lemma-reduction-derived-nakayama]) therefore reduces us
to showing $C/\pi_E=0$. In other words, we must show that the reduction
of the projection formula map is an isomorphism.

This reduction is the torsion projection formula map, which is an
isomorphism by [Stacks, [0F0G](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0G)]. To identify the two maps, note that the
sources and targets correspond by $\rho_K$ and
associativity of extension of scalars, and the maps agree because both are
adjoint to the counit $p^*Rp_*K\to K$, as is
$\rho_K$.

*Rational coefficients.* Here $Rp_*$ commutes with the operations that
produce the generators of Lemma [lemma-integral-models](4) from
integral complexes. For $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the complex
$K[1/\ell]$ is the colimit of $K\xrightarrow{\ell}K\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots$,
and since this system has a common lower bound,
Corollary [corollary-continuity-cohomology] shows that

$$
Rp_*(K[1/\ell])\simeq(Rp_*K)[1/\ell].
$$

Likewise $Rp_*$ commutes with extension of scalars to a finite
$E'/E$, which is a finite direct sum by
Lemma [lemma-inverse-image-coefficient-sheaves](2). By
Corollary [corollary-continuity-cohomology] again, it also commutes with the filtered colimit
$\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}-=\varinjlim_{E'}E'_X\otimes_{E_X}-$.
By the integral case, it follows that $Rp_*$ maps the generators
into $\Dbc(Y,E)$ and $\Dbc(Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$. Since $Rp_*$ is exact and $\Dbc(Y,E)$
and $\Dbc(Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ are triangulated
(Corollary [corollary-coefficient-heart-b]), $Rp_*$ preserves
$\Dbc(-,E)$ and $\Dbc(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$.

For proper base change and the projection formula it is enough to treat
the generators. Indeed, both sides of each map are exact functors in each
variable, so the objects for which the map is an isomorphism form a
triangulated subcategory. On the generators, the maps are obtained from
the integral isomorphisms by inverting $\ell$ and extending scalars. These
operations commute with $Rp_*$ by the preceding paragraph, and with $g^*$
and $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$ because they are given by tensoring with the
coefficient sheaves. Moreover, the maps so obtained are the base change and
projection formula maps, since these scalar comparisons commute with the
counits of $p^*\dashv Rp_*$.

Apply Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-finite-coefficients] to the proper morphism $p$ and $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},A)$. That proposition gives bounded constructible cohomology and the finite Tor-amplitude bound for $Rp_{*,A}K$. These are precisely the conditions for membership in $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},A)$.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-constructible-complexes].

sources and targets correspond by (4.15) and

For each functor we need two facts: it preserves direct sums, and it
maps $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ into $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}$. The rest then follows from the definition of
the localizing categories, in the form recalled before the proposition.

For $Rp_*$ with $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, Lemma [lemma-proper-direct-image-unbounded-complexes](3)
shows that $Rp_*$ preserves direct sums on
$\Dic(X,\Lambda)\supset\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))$, and
Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-constructible-complexes] shows that $Rp_*$ preserves

Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-finite-coefficients] and
Corollary [corollary-proper-direct-image-finite-coefficients-localizing];
for $\mathcal O_E$, they are
Proposition [proposition-compactness-proper-direct-image] and Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-constructible-complexes]. In each case, the
objects
$K\in\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))$ with
$Rp_*K\in\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y,\Lambda))$ form a triangulated subcategory closed
under direct sums and containing $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$, and hence they form all of
$\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))$.

Extension by zero is exact and left adjoint to $j^*$, so it preserves
direct sums. It preserves constructibility, since we may add the closed
complement as a stratum on which the sheaf is zero. For finite $A$ it also preserves finite Tor amplitude, as one checks on stalks, while for $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ we have $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}=\Dbc$, so constructibility
suffices; for $\mathcal O_E$ this is Lemma [lemma-inverse-image-tensor-product]. With this, the localizing-subcategory argument shows that $j_!$ restricts as stated.

For $Rp_*$ with $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, Lemma [lemma-proper-direct-image-unbounded-complexes](3)
shows that $Rp_*$ preserves direct sums on
$\Dic(X,\Lambda)\supset\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))$, and
Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-constructible-complexes] shows that $Rp_*$ preserves
$D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}=\Dbc$. For finite $A$, these two facts are
Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-finite-coefficients] and
Corollary [corollary-proper-direct-image-finite-coefficients-localizing];
for $\mathcal O_E$, they are
Proposition [proposition-compactness-proper-direct-image] and Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-constructible-complexes]. In each case, the
objects
$K\in\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))$ with
$Rp_*K\in\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y,\Lambda))$ form a triangulated subcategory closed
under direct sums and containing $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$, and hence they form all of
$\Loc(D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))$.

By Corollary [corollary-finite-tor-amplitude-under-comparison] the
étale and pro-étale categories $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ agree, and by
Theorem [theorem-comparison-direct-images] so do the proper direct
images of their bounded below complexes. We can therefore transport bounded constructibility and the Tor bound
from the étale site.

On the étale site, let $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\acute{e}t},A)$. The proper
direct image of a constructible torsion sheaf is constructible
[Stacks, [0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0)], and $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(p)<\infty$
[Stacks, [0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10)]. Hence $Rp_*C\in\Dbc(Y_{\acute{e}t},A)$.

To check finite Tor amplitude, suppose that $C$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, and let
$d$ be an integer with $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(X_{\bar y})\leq d$ for
all geometric points $\bar y$ of $Y$. Since derived tensor products are computed
stalkwise, it suffices to show that each stalk $(Rp_*C)_{\bar y}$ has
Tor amplitude in $[a,b+d]$ as a complex of $A$-modules. In other words,
$(Rp_*C)_{\bar y}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AN=((Rp_*C)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_Y)_{\bar y}$
should have cohomology in $[a,b+d]$ for every $A$-module $N$. By proper base change
and the projection formula for constant modules [Stacks, [0F12](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F12)], this stalk is

$$
R\Gamma\bigl(X_{\bar y},
C|_{X_{\bar y}}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_{X_{\bar y}}\bigr).
$$

The complex $C|_{X_{\bar y}}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_{X_{\bar y}}$ has
cohomology in $[a,b]$, because restriction to the fibre preserves Tor
amplitude. Since $R\Gamma(X_{\bar y},-)$ preserves $D^{\geq a}$ and has
cohomological dimension at most $d$, it keeps the lower bound and raises the upper bound by
at most $d$. Thus $Rp_*C\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y_{\acute{e}t},A)$, with Tor amplitude in $[a,b+d]$.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-finite-coefficients], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

Everything follows from the chain formula, which we prove first by
writing evaluation and coevaluation in a finite dual basis.
If $e_1,\dots,e_n$ and $e^1,\dots,e^n$ are dual
bases of $A^n$ and its dual, then $\operatorname{coev}(1)=\sum_je_j\otimes e^j$,
and the composite of the definition sends $1$ to
$\sum_je^j(v(e_j))$, the ordinary trace of a matrix. The same computation
applies to a finite projective module, which is a direct summand of such an $A^n$.
On a complex, the symmetry interchanging a term
of degree $i$ and its dual of degree $-i$ contributes $(-1)^i$, which
proves the chain formula. Its right-hand side is invariant under chain
homotopy, since the supertrace of $dh+hd$ is zero by cyclicity and a shift of
index.

Tensoring a dual basis with $B$ preserves evaluation and coevaluation. Hence
the trace is compatible with extension of scalars for every ring map
$A\to B$. Linearity and invariance under conjugacy follow from the same description. For additivity, note that a two-step filtered object of the filtered derived category may be
represented by a filtered complex of projective modules whose filtration is
split in each degree. The endomorphism is then block triangular, so its
supertrace is the sum of the supertraces on the two graded pieces. Finally, over a field the boundaries
$B^i$ and cycles $Z^i$ are $v$-invariant subspaces
$B^i\subset Z^i\subset P^i$, with $Z^i/B^i=H^i(P)$, and the
differential induces a $v$-equivariant isomorphism $P^i/Z^i\simeq B^{i+1}$.
Hence

$$
\operatorname{Tr}(v^i\mid P^i)=\operatorname{Tr}(v\mid B^i)
+\operatorname{Tr}(H^i(v)\mid H^i(P))+\operatorname{Tr}(v\mid B^{i+1}),
$$

and in the alternating sum the terms for the $B^i$ cancel in pairs,
leaving the cohomological formula.

In the evaluation–coevaluation definition the endomorphism $v$ occurs exactly once. Tensoring and composition are $A$-linear in this entry. Replacing $v$ by $av+bw$ therefore replaces its trace by $a\operatorname{tr}(v)+b\operatorname{tr}(w)$.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-properties-trace].

An isomorphism $u:P\to Q$ transports the duality maps by $u$ on the object and $(u^{-1})^\vee$ on its dual. Insert these transports into the composite defining the trace of $uvu^{-1}$. The adjacent $u^{-1}u$ and their duals cancel, leaving the composite defining the trace of $v$.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-properties-trace].

Write $\phi_{Q,Q'}:F(Q)\otimes F(Q')\xrightarrow{\sim}F(Q\otimes Q')$ for the
monoidal structure of $F$ and $\beta$ for the braidings, so that
$F(\beta_{Q,Q'})\circ\phi_{Q,Q'}=\phi_{Q',Q}\circ\beta_{F(Q),F(Q')}$. Since $F$
is an additive functor, $a\mapsto F(a)$ is additive and multiplicative on
$\operatorname{End}(\mathbf 1_{\mathcal C})$ and preserves $1$, and conjugation
by $\phi_0$ preserves these properties. So $\rho_F$ is a ring map.

*The trace does not depend on the right dual.* Let $(P^\vee,\mathrm{ev},
\mathrm{coev})$ and $(Q,\mathrm{ev}_Q,\mathrm{coev}_Q)$ be right duals of $P$,
with $\mathrm{ev}:P^\vee\otimes P\to\mathbf 1$ and
$\mathrm{coev}:\mathbf 1\to P\otimes P^\vee$ as in
Definition [definition-categorical-trace--2]. The composite
$u:P^\vee\to P^\vee\otimes P\otimes Q\to Q$ of $1\otimes\mathrm{coev}_Q$ and
$\mathrm{ev}\otimes1$ (with the unit and associativity constraints) is an
isomorphism, and the triangle identities give
$\mathrm{ev}_Q\circ(u\otimes1_P)=\mathrm{ev}$ and
$(1_P\otimes u)\circ\mathrm{coev}=\mathrm{coev}_Q$. Using these and the
naturality of $\beta$,

$$
\mathrm{ev}_Q\circ\beta_{P,Q}\circ(v\otimes1_Q)\circ\mathrm{coev}_Q
=\mathrm{ev}_Q\circ\beta_{P,Q}\circ(1_P\otimes u)\circ(v\otimes1)\circ\mathrm{coev}
=\mathrm{ev}_Q\circ(u\otimes1_P)\circ\beta_{P,P^\vee}\circ(v\otimes1)\circ\mathrm{coev},
$$

which is the trace computed with $P^\vee$.

*Transport of the dual.* Put
$\mathrm{ev}'=\phi_0^{-1}\circ F(\mathrm{ev})\circ\phi_{P^\vee,P}$ and
$\mathrm{coev}'=\phi_{P,P^\vee}^{-1}\circ F(\mathrm{coev})\circ\phi_0$.
Applying $F$ to the two triangle identities of $(P,P^\vee)$ and using the
naturality of $\phi$ and its compatibility with the associativity and unit
constraints gives the triangle identities for $(\mathrm{ev}',\mathrm{coev}')$,
so $F(P^\vee)$ with these maps is a right dual of $F(P)$. With this dual, the
braided compatibility of $\phi$ and its naturality,
$\phi_{P,P^\vee}\circ(F(v)\otimes1)=F(v\otimes1)\circ\phi_{P,P^\vee}$, give

$$
\mathrm{ev}'\circ\beta_{F(P),F(P^\vee)}\circ(F(v)\otimes1)\circ\mathrm{coev}'
=\phi_0^{-1}\circ F\bigl(\mathrm{ev}\circ\beta_{P,P^\vee}\circ(v\otimes1)
\circ\mathrm{coev}\bigr)\circ\phi_0
=\rho_F(\operatorname{tr}(v\mid P)).
$$

By the previous paragraph, the left side is $\operatorname{tr}(F(v)\mid F(P))$
for any right dual of $F(P)$. By conjugacy invariance
(clause [proposition-properties-trace--2]) applied to $e$,
$\operatorname{tr}(v'\mid P')=\operatorname{tr}(F(v)\mid F(P))$, which proves
the formula.

*Scalar extension.* Let $A\to B$ be a ring map, and represent perfect
complexes by bounded complexes of finite projective modules, so that derived
tensor products are total tensor products. Then $F=-\otimes_AB$ is an additive
functor from perfect $A$-complexes to perfect $B$-complexes. The isomorphisms
$(M\otimes_AB)\otimes_B(N\otimes_AB)\to(M\otimes_AN)\otimes_AB$,
$(m\otimes b)\otimes(n\otimes b')\mapsto(m\otimes n)\otimes bb'$, and
$B\simeq A\otimes_AB$ make it strong monoidal. It is braided because both
symmetries carry the same Koszul sign $(-1)^{|m||n|}$. The endomorphism rings
of the units are $A$ and $B$, with $a$ acting by multiplication, and
$F(a)$ is multiplication by the image of $a$ in $B$, so $\rho_F$ is the given
map $A\to B$. Every perfect complex has the right dual $P^\vee$ of
Definition [definition-categorical-trace--1]. Taking $P'=F(P)$, $e=\mathrm{id}$ and
$v'=v\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ gives the last assertion.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-properties-trace].

Let $B^i\subset Z^i\subset P^i$ be the boundaries and cycles. They are stable under $v$, with quotients $Z^i/B^i=H^i(P)$ and $P^i/Z^i\simeq B^{i+1}$ equivariantly. The idea is to produce one
trivial sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $A\times A\times A$ by the theorem of the
cube, and to pull it back
along maps $A\to A\times A\times A$ chosen so that the result is a
relation between $[n+1]^*\mathcal L$, $[n]^*\mathcal L$ and
$[n-1]^*\mathcal L$. The theorem of the cube applies because $A$ is
geometrically integral (Lemma [lemma-abelian-variety-commutative]).

Consider
on $A\times A\times A$ the invertible sheaf

$$
\mathcal M=m_{123}^*\mathcal L\otimes m_{12}^*\mathcal L^{-1}\otimes
m_{13}^*\mathcal L^{-1}\otimes m_{23}^*\mathcal L^{-1}\otimes
p_1^*\mathcal L\otimes p_2^*\mathcal L\otimes p_3^*\mathcal L,
$$

where the $p_i$ are the projections and $m_{12}$, $m_{13}$, $m_{23}$,
$m_{123}$ are the sums of the indicated coordinates. To apply the
theorem of the cube, we restrict $\mathcal M$ to the three slices. On
$e\times A\times A$, with coordinates $(x_2,x_3)$, the seven factors
restrict to $\mathcal L$ pulled back along $x_2+x_3$, $x_2$, $x_3$,
$x_2+x_3$, the constant map $e$, $x_2$ and $x_3$, with exponents
$1,-1,-1,-1,1,1,1$. Of these, the pullback along the constant map is trivial, and the others cancel. The same holds on $A\times e\times A$ and
$A\times A\times e$. Hence $\mathcal M$ is trivial by
Theorem [theorem-theorem-cube]. Finally, pulling the trivial sheaf $\mathcal M$ back along
$x\mapsto(x,x,[n-1]x)$ for $n\ge0$ yields

$$
[n+1]^*\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes2}
\otimes[n-1]^*\mathcal L
\simeq [2]^*\mathcal L\otimes([n]^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes2}.
$$

To see this, note that the composites of $x\mapsto(x,x,[n-1]x)$ with
$m_{123}$, $m_{12}$, $m_{13}$, $m_{23}$, $p_1$, $p_2$, $p_3$ are
$[n+1]$, $[2]$, $[n]$, $[n]$, $\mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{id}$, $[n-1]$.
The cases $n=0$ and $n=1$ of the formula are clear. For $n=0$, since
$[0]^*\mathcal L$ is trivial, the relation reads
$\mathcal L^{\otimes3}\otimes[-1]^*\mathcal L\simeq[2]^*\mathcal L$.
This is the case $n=2$ of the formula. In general, the relation
expresses $[n+1]^*\mathcal L$ in terms of $[n]^*\mathcal L$ and
$[n-1]^*\mathcal L$, and the exponents in the formula satisfy the same
second order recursion. Induction on $n$ therefore gives the formula [Stacks, [0BFF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFF)].
In particular, for symmetric $\mathcal N$ the two exponents add up to $n^2$.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-pullback-multiplication-n], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-pullback-multiplication-n], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

We twist to weight zero and add the dual, as in
Proposition [proposition-twisting-weight-zero-adding-dual], before taking the transform, so
that a twist of $M'$ becomes a quotient of a real sheaf, to which
Theorem [theorem-purity-real-sheaves-curves] applies.

Choose $b$ as in
Proposition [proposition-twisting-weight-zero-adding-dual], so that
$M^0=M\otimes\mathcal B_b$ is pure of weight zero.

On the product of the line and the dual line, consider the sheaf

$$
F=
(p_1^*j_!M^0\otimes\mathcal K_\psi)
\ \oplus\
(p_1^*j_!(M^0)^\vee\otimes\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}).
$$

At each closed point, the Frobenius eigenvalues of the second summand
are the complex conjugates of those of the first, because the
eigenvalues of $M^0$ have absolute value one and those of the
character sheaves are roots of unity, while at the boundary both zero
extensions have zero stalks. Hence $F$ is real, as in
Lemma [lemma-twisted-envelope]. Moreover, since
duality replaces $a$ by $-a$, the dual $(M^0)^\vee$ also has no
geometric constituent of the form $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}$, so the argument of
Lemma [lemma-fourier-transform-boundary-sequence] shows
that the direct image with compact support of $F$ along $p_2$ is
concentrated in degree one. We set $H=R^1p_{2!}F$.

Let $y$ be a point with values in a finite field. Since
$Rp_{2!}F=H[-1]$, the trace formula for $Rp_{2!}$
(Corollary [corollary-trace-functions-direct-image-compact]) gives
$-t_H(y)=\sum_x t_F(x,y)$. For each $x$ the traces of the two
summands of $F$ at $(x,y)$ are complex conjugate, so $t_H(y)$ is
real. Over the finite extensions of $\kappa(y)$ the same argument
shows that the trace of every power of the local
Frobenius is real. These traces are the power sums of the local
eigenvalues, and the Newton identities express the coefficients of
the characteristic polynomial through the power sums with rational
coefficients. Hence the local characteristic polynomials of $H$ have
real coefficients, that is, $H$ is real.

The first summand of $H$ is
$R^1p_{2!}(p_1^*j_!M\otimes\mathcal K_\psi)\otimes\mathcal B_b$ by the
projection formula for the constant twist, that is, $G\otimes\mathcal B_b$
with $G=\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!M)$ as in
Lemma [lemma-fourier-transform-boundary-sequence]. Tensoring the surjection
$G\to j'_*M'$ of that lemma with $\mathcal B_b$, we see that
$M'\otimes\mathcal B_b$ is a quotient of a direct summand of $H$.
To apply the purity theorem we restrict to a dense open on which both $H$ and $M'$ are lisse.
There $M'\otimes\mathcal B_b$ is a lisse quotient of the real lisse
sheaf $H$, and it is irreducible by Lemma [lemma-simple-objects],
so by Theorem [theorem-purity-real-sheaves-curves] it is
pure of some real weight. Removing the
twist by $\mathcal B_b$, we find that $M'$ is pure of some weight $v$
on that open. Since the open where $M'$ is lisse is a smooth
geometrically connected curve, the last assertion of
Corollary [corollary-unramified-boundary-point] extends the purity to
all of it.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-purity-lisse-part-fourier-transform], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

Both identities are instances of base change for smooth purity, applied
to a square whose horizontal maps are not $k$-linear. Since $\gamma_f$
and $\operatorname{Tr}_f$ are built from base change maps and from the

acts on Kummer classes.

The first identity is Proposition [proposition-compatibility-purity-base-change] for this
square. Since $\operatorname{Fr}_X$ is not a morphism over $k$, the only
point to check is that the identification of twists used there is the

$\operatorname{Fr}_T$ sends the Kummer class of a unit to the Kummer class

together give the statement for $\operatorname{Tr}_f$.

We transport the trace map of affine space along local trivializations,
show that the result does not depend on the trivialization, so that the
local maps glue to a trace isomorphism $\operatorname{Tr}_\pi$ for $V$, and
take the map $\pi^*K(d)[2d]\to\pi^!K$ to be its adjoint.

*Local trace maps.* Locally on $S$ the bundle is affine space, where
the trace map has already been constructed. Over an open $U\subset S$ on
which $V$ is trivial, a trivialization
$\tau:V\times_S U\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf A^d_U$
transports (9.11) to an isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{\tau}:
R(\pi|_{V\times_S U})_!(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_{V\times_S U}(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_U.
$$

These maps commute with base change in $U$, because the construction uses
only $c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_U}(1))$, the splitting
(9.8) and localization at infinity: pullback
preserves the Kummer class, and proper base change and localization
identify the pullbacks of the constructions with those over the new base.

*Independence of the trivialization.* A change of trivialization
multiplies the trace map by a locally constant unit on $\GL_d$, and this
unit is $1$. As two trivializations differ by a matrix with values in
$\GL_d$, it suffices to study one universal change of coordinates,
parametrized by $\GL_{d,S}$ itself, and then pull back. Let

$$
\theta:\mathbf A^d_{\GL_{d,S}}\longrightarrow\mathbf A^d_{\GL_{d,S}},
\qquad (g,v)\longmapsto(g,gv),
$$

be the universal linear change of coordinates, an automorphism over
$\GL_{d,S}$. It induces an automorphism of the compactly supported
direct image of $(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_{\mathbf A^d_{\GL_{d,S}}}(d)[2d]$
to $\GL_{d,S}$, which the trace map identifies with the constant sheaf
$(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_{\GL_{d,S}}$ in degree zero, so that this
automorphism is multiplication by a section

$$
u\in H^0\bigl((\GL_{d,S})_{\acute{e}t},
(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_{\GL_{d,S}}^{\times}\bigr),
$$

a locally constant function with values in
$(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)^{\times}$. It is therefore constant on each geometric
fibre $\GL_{d,\bar s}$, which is connected: for $d\geq1$ it
is a nonempty open subset of the affine space of $d\times d$ matrices,
and for $d=0$ it is a point. As $\theta$ is the identity at the identity
matrix, which lies on every geometric fibre, $u=1$.

The local trace maps agree on overlaps of trivializing opens. Indeed, let
$\tau$ and $\tau'$ be two trivializations over $U$. Then
$\tau'\circ\tau^{-1}$ is the pullback of $\theta$ along the transition
matrix $U\to\GL_{d,S}$, so by base change the equality $u=1$ implies
$\operatorname{Tr}_{\tau'}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\tau}$. Moreover, morphisms between
source and target form a sheaf, as both are locally sheaves in degree zero.
Hence the local maps glue over a trivializing cover to an isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{\pi}:
R\pi_!(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_V(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_S.
$$

*The map $\pi^*K(d)[2d]\to\pi^!K$.* For general $K$, the projection formula and
$\operatorname{Tr}_\pi$ give

$$
R\pi_!\bigl(\pi^{*}K(d)[2d]\bigr)
\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L} R\pi_!(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_V(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{id}_K\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{\pi}\ }K.
$$

Its adjoint under $R\pi_!\dashv\pi^{!}$
(Proposition [proposition-exceptional-inverse-image-smooth-morphism](1)) is the asserted map.
We show that it is an isomorphism. This may be checked locally on $V$,
because $\pi^!$ commutes with restriction to opens. Over each trivializing
open, $\operatorname{Tr}_\pi$ is $\operatorname{Tr}_\tau$ by construction,
so there the map is the isomorphism given by the adjunction for
affine space following (9.11).
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-purity-vector-bundles], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

We stratify the target so that over each stratum, $G$ is lisse off a
subscheme that is finite over the base. On the lisse part the
projection is a relative affine curve, and we apply
Theorem [theorem-pure-lisse-sheaves-over-relative]. On the finite
part it is quasi-finite, and we apply
Lemma [lemma-finite-quasi-finite-direct-images].

Take a finite mixed filtration of $G$. In the long exact
sequences of $R^ip_!$ for its steps, the bound $w+i$ passes from the
pure quotients to $G$ by Lemma [lemma-weights-exact-sequence]. We
may therefore assume that $G$ is pure and constructible of weight
$v\leq w$.

Suppose first that the target $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is integral
and affine, so that $\mathbf A^1_{Y_0}$ is integral. We construct the
strata as follows. Choose a dense open $U$ on which $G$ is lisse. Since the
locus where $G$ is lisse is stable under Frobenius, we may replace
$U$ by the intersection of its finitely many Frobenius conjugates. Then
$U$ is defined over $k_0$, and so are the ideal $I\subset R[T]$ of its
reduced complement and the choices below. If the complement is
nonempty, choose a nonzero $g\in I$ and invert its nonzero leading
coefficient $b$. Then over $R_b$ the polynomial $b^{-1}g$ is monic and
vanishes in $R_b[T]/I$. Hence the image of $T$ is integral over $R_b$,
and $R_b[T]/I$ is generated as an $R_b$-module by the powers $T^k$ with
$k<\deg g$. In particular $R_b[T]/I$ is finite over $R_b$; if $g$ has
degree zero, the complement is empty over $D(b)$.

Over $D(b)$ the complement is therefore finite, hence quasi-finite. The
open $U$ is smooth of relative dimension one over $D(b)$, and each of its
fibres is an affine line minus finitely many points. So $U\to D(b)$
satisfies the hypotheses of
Theorem [theorem-pure-lisse-sheaves-over-relative]. Applying that
theorem on $U$ and
Lemma [lemma-finite-quasi-finite-direct-images] on the complement,
we obtain the bound over $D(b)$ from
Lemma [lemma-weight-bounds-partitions](1).

For a general target we argue by induction on $\dim Y_0$. Since
nilpotents do not change the étale site, we may replace $Y_0$ by its
reduction. Take disjoint integral affine opens containing the generic
points of its components, and perform this construction on each of
them. Their union is open, and its complement has smaller dimension.
The case of dimension zero is contained in the construction, because a
reduced zero-dimensional scheme is a finite disjoint union of integral
affine pieces. In general, the restriction of $G$ over the closed
complement is again mixed of weights at most $w$, and the inductive
hypothesis gives the bound there.
Lemma [lemma-weight-bounds-partitions](2), applied to the open
union and its closed complement in the target, gives the bound over
all of $Y_0$.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-relative-affine-line], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

We define the isomorphism as a chain of three steps: restrict $\omega_f$ to
the diagonal of $X\times_YX$, move the diagonal to the zero section of
$T_{X/Y}$, and use the orientation of a vector bundle.

The projection $p_1$ is the base change of $f$ along $f$, so
Proposition [proposition-exceptional-inverse-image-smooth-morphism](3) shows that
$\omega_{p_1}\simeq p_2^{*}\omega_f$. Since $p_2\circ\Delta$ is the
identity of $X$, we get the first isomorphism in

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega_{f}
&\simeq L\Delta^{*}\omega_{p_1}
\xrightarrow{\sim}z^{*}\omega_{\pi}
\xrightarrow{\sim}z^{*}(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d]
\simeq(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_{X}(d)[2d].
\end{aligned}

The second isomorphism is Lemma [lemma-section-normal-bundle] for the section

isomorphism of Proposition [proposition-purity-vector-bundles]
at the constant sheaf, applied to the vector bundle $T_{X/Y}$ over $X$.

Since each step is attached to $f$ without choices, the composite is

This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-relative-dualizing-complex], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

The scheme $T_0$ is the normalization of $T$ in $Z$, that is, the
relative spectrum of the integral closure of $\mathcal O_T$ in the
direct image of $\mathcal O_Z$; it is affine over $T$ by
construction. By Zariski's Main Theorem in the form [Stacks, [02LR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02LR)], locally on $T$
the canonical map from $Z$ to the normalization $T_0$ of $T$ in $Z$ is
an open immersion, and $T_0\to T$ is affine. These factorizations agree
on overlaps and glue to the stated factorization. Over an affine open of $T$ the scheme $T_0$ is
affine, so $Z$ is a quasi-compact open of an affine scheme there,
which means that $Z\to T$ is quasi-affine.

Evaluate the sequence on a weakly contractible $W$. Since every
epimorphism of sheaves is surjective on sections over $W$, the transition
maps $F_{n+1}(W)\to F_n(W)$ are surjective. Given a section at stage $m$,
we choose lifts successively at stages $m+1,m+2,\ldots$ (by countable
choice), while the earlier stages are determined by the transition maps.
This gives a compatible section of $\varprojlim_nF_n(W)$. Since limits
are computed on sections, the projection is surjective on $W$.

[bhatt-scholze15, §§3.1–3.2].

We treat the operations in the order in which they depend on each other:
first the local operations $f^*$ and $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$, then the two
direct images, and finally internal Hom, which we express through the
others.

Pullback and tensor product preserve the property of being, on the strata
of a finite stratification, locally $\Lambda_S\otimes P$ with $P$ a perfect
complex. For pullback this is clear, since the strata pull back to a stratification, while for tensor products we take a common refinement of the two
stratifications, and on each of its strata we use that
$P\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q$ is perfect when $P$ and $Q$ are. Similarly, extension by zero preserves finite Tor amplitude, since it is exact and satisfies the
projection formula $a_!K\otimes^{\mathbf L}N\simeq a_!(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^*N)$.
Concretely, for finite $A$ these statements can be checked on the bounded flat
constructible models of Lemma [lemma-flat-models-generators]. For $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, on the other hand, they follow from Lemma [lemma-inverse-image-tensor-product] and from Definition [definition-constructible-sheaves] of constructible sheaves: on each stratum, such a sheaf is
locally $\Lambda_X\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$ with $P$ finitely generated over
the discrete valuation ring or field $\Lambda(*)$. Over such a ring a finitely generated module has a finite free resolution of length at most
one. Hence $P$ is perfect.

For the direct images we use a compactification to separate the proper
part from the open part. Proper direct image preserves $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(-,\Lambda)$ by
Proposition [proposition-proper-direct-image-constructible-complexes]. Direct image along an open
immersion preserves it by Proposition [proposition-open-direct-image-preserves-finite] for finite $A$ and
Proposition [proposition-direct-image-along-open-immersion] for $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.
If $f=pj$ is a compactification, then $Rf_*=Rp_*Rj_*$ and
$Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$. Each of these composites consists of functors already
known to preserve $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}$, which proves both assertions on direct images. That $f^!$
preserves $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(-,\Lambda)$ is part of Theorem [theorem-exceptional-inverse-image].

For internal Hom we reduce to a
first argument supported on a single stratum, where $\cHom$ can be
written in terms of $Ra_*$, $a^!$ and $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.
This is possible because the functor $\cHom(-,K)$ sends triangles in the first argument to triangles, and $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ is closed under cones and shifts. Hence, for a
triangle $M'\to M\to M''$, the complex $\cHom(M,K)$ lies in $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}$
whenever $\cHom(M',K)$ and $\cHom(M'',K)$ do. Using a finite
stratification and finite cones, we may therefore reduce to the case where
the first argument is $a_!P$. Here $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is locally closed
and $P$ is a locally constant perfect complex on $S$. For finite $A$ this reduction follows from the bounded flat model and its stupid filtration, and for $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ it follows from the same description of
constructible sheaves on strata. By tensor-Hom adjunction and the
projection formula for $a_!$ we have

$$
\cHom_X(a_!P,K)
\simeq Ra_*\cHom_S(P,a^!K)
\simeq Ra_*(P^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^!K).
$$

Pulling back the Kummer sequence of $C_{\acute{e}t}$ by $\nu_C^*$, we get
the exact sequence of sheaves on $C_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$

$$
0\longrightarrow\mu_n\longrightarrow\nu_C^*\mathbf G_m
\xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n}\nu_C^*\mathbf G_m
\longrightarrow0.
$$

Here surjectivity of the $n$th power map is a local question. For a
unit $a$ the equation $T^n=a$ defines an étale cover, since its
derivative $nT^{n-1}$ is a unit. Moreover, the global units on the proper connected curve form the group $k^\times$, which is
$n$-divisible because $k$ is algebraically closed. Hence the long exact
sequence starts with $H^0(C,\mu_n)=\mu_n(k)$. Since the map
$H^0(C,\mathbf G_m)\to H^0(C,\mathbf G_m)$ is onto, $H^1(C,\mu_n)$
injects into $H^1(C,\mathbf G_m)$. Using
Lemma [lemma-cohomology-multiplicative-group], we read off from the
long exact sequence that

$$
H^1(C,\mu_n)=\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n],\qquad
H^2(C,\mu_n)=\operatorname{Pic}(C)/n,
$$

with all higher groups zero.

Corollary [corollary-degree-jacobian] gives the exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow J(C)(k)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(C)
\xrightarrow{\deg}\mathbf Z\longrightarrow0.
$$

Multiplication by $n$ on $J(C)(k)$ is surjective, with kernel
$J(C)[n](k)$, and $J(C)[n]$ is finite étale of rank $n^{2g}$
(Corollary [corollary-torsion-jacobian-field-extension]).  Applying the snake lemma to
multiplication by $n$ on this sequence, and using that $\mathbf Z$ is
torsion free, we obtain $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]=J(C)[n](k)$ and
$\operatorname{Pic}(C)/n=\mathbf Z/n$ via the degree. In particular,
$H^1(C,\mu_n)$ is noncanonically isomorphic to $(\mathbf Z/n)^{2g}$
[Stacks, [03RQ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RQ)].

Under an algebraically closed extension $k'/k$, the schemes $J(C)$ and $J(C)[n]$
base change to the corresponding objects for $C_{k'}$. The map
$J(C)[n](k)\to J(C)[n](k')$ is bijective by
Corollary [corollary-torsion-jacobian-field-extension]. The same argument
applies to the finite étale scheme $\mu_n$. Finally, pullback of line
bundles preserves the degree. Hence the pullback maps on cohomology are
isomorphisms.

and every ingredient in it extends along $\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z\to A$,
where we choose $n$ with $\ell^nA=0$. Once the Kummer and diagonal classes are
extended, the calculation works with $A$ throughout. In particular, the splitting for the
projective line has two free summands, and its integration and triangle
identities keep the same normalization, since
(9.9) is an identity of endomorphisms of a
constant sheaf and is preserved by extension of scalars. So the local
adjunctions compute $f_A^!$, and the arguments for vector bundles and

$$
f_A^{*}K\otimes^{\mathbf L}A_X(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\sim}f_A^{*}K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\omega_{f,A}
\xrightarrow{\sim}f_A^{!}K.
$$

and both are natural in $K$.

We repeat the construction of Section [sec-The-trace-map-of-affine-space] in the topos of towers. The construction
has two parts: on a chart we write down an explicit adjunction, built from
the trace of the projective line, and then we glue these local adjunctions
over a finite cover. The gluing is done with pairs consisting of an object
and a counit, as in Definition [definition-representing-objects], because such
pairs are unique up to unique isomorphism and so need no choice of
transition maps.

The Kummer sequence
$0\to(\mu_{\ell^n})_n\to(\mathbf G_m,(\cdot)^\ell)\to(\mathbf G_m,\mathrm{id})\to0$ is exact
in towers. Hence Chern classes, the diagonal class and the trace of the
projective line are single morphisms of towers. Moreover, the identities
(9.9) are equalities of maps between
sheaves of towers in degree zero, so they can be checked at each level.
The construction of (9.10) then gives the adjunction for the
projective line in $D(\operatorname{Tow})$, and extension by zero and the
étale adjunction give local adjunctions on charts.

We glue the local adjunctions in $D(\operatorname{Tow})$, by induction on a
finite cover. Let $X=U\cup V$, and let $(H_U,\varepsilon_U)$ and
$(H_V,\varepsilon_V)$ be pairs representing $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,\bullet}(-),K_\bullet)$
on $U$ and on $V$. Put $W=U\cap V$. Both pairs restrict to pairs
representing this functor on $W$, so by Yoneda there is a unique
counit-preserving isomorphism between the restrictions, and we call the
common restriction $H_W$. Let $H$ be the cone of
$j_{W!}H_W\to j_{U!}H_U\oplus j_{V!}H_V$, as in the triangle
(9.12). Since the counits $\varepsilon_U,\varepsilon_V$
agree on $Rf_{!,\bullet}j_{W!}H_W$, the exact Hom sequence shows that they
lift to a counit $\varepsilon:Rf_{!,\bullet}H\to K_\bullet$. The
five lemma, applied as in the finite case, then shows that $(H,\varepsilon)$
represents $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,\bullet}(-),K_\bullet)$ on $X$. The
tower $H$ is also constructible. Indeed, $H|_U\simeq H_U$ and $H|_V\simeq H_V$,
so the union of their intervals bounds its cohomology and Tor amplitude
uniformly in $n$.

Repeating this step over a finite cover of $X$ by charts gives a pair
representing $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,\bullet}(-),K_\bullet)$ on all of
$X$, and we let $f^!_\bullet K_\bullet$ be its object. By uniqueness of
representing pairs, this is functorial in $K_\bullet$ and gives the
adjunction (9.18).

The levels are the finite ones, because evaluation at level $n$ carries the
glued pair to a pair representing $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!(-),K_n)$ with
coefficients $\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Indeed, on each chart it is the local
finite adjunction, and the five lemma argument applies at level $n$, so by
uniqueness this pair is the finite one. As the counit is one morphism of
towers, it commutes with the transition maps, and transposing this identity
gives the reduction maps.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-sp-tower-geometric], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

We first replace $B$ by an ind-Zariski $B$-algebra, so
that its spectrum is w-local and its closed points lie exactly over the
closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$; such a refinement does not
change the local rings.
Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ lie over a closed point $\mathfrak m$ of
$\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Since $R_{\mathfrak m}$ is strictly henselian,
the ind-étale local homomorphism $R_{\mathfrak m}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$
is an isomorphism. Hence every component of $\operatorname{Spec}(B)$
maps isomorphically onto the component of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ below
it, and a retraction amounts to a continuous choice of one component above each component of
$\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Such a choice exists because, by Proposition [proposition-gleason-s-theorem], the surjection
$\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}(B))\to\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}(R))$ of
profinite component spaces has a section.
Given such a section, we restrict $B$ to the corresponding closed set of components by a
filtered colimit of localizations at idempotents. The result is an
$R$-algebra isomorphic to $R$, and this gives the retraction. For details

There are two things to check: that the coverings form a subcanonical
topology, and that base change of objects is a morphism of sites.

Identity covers, composites of covers, and base changes of covers are
again covers. For the underlying morphisms this is
Lemma [lemma-stability], and for the finite refinement
condition it is part of the fpqc covering axioms. Representable presheaves
satisfy descent for these covers by fpqc descent for morphisms of
schemes, so they are sheaves, and the topology is subcanonical.

For $f:X\to Y$, the functor $V\mapsto V\times_YX$ sends weakly étale
$Y$-schemes to weakly étale $X$-schemes by
Lemma [lemma-stability]. It preserves fibre products and
the final object, hence finite limits, and it carries covering families
to covering families because fpqc coverings are stable under base change.
Such a functor defines a geometric morphism, whose inverse image $f^{-1}$
is left exact and, as a left adjoint, preserves all colimits. Exactness
on abelian sheaves follows, and compatibility with composition holds
because $(V\times_ZY)\times_YX\simeq V\times_ZX$ canonically. This is the
small-site version of the constructions in [Stacks, [0988](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0988)].

Each trace map is a map $\gamma$ followed by a counit. The maps $\gamma$
compose by Proposition [proposition-compatibility-purity-composition],
and the counits compose because the counit of a composite adjunction is the
composite of the counits, so the only thing to arrange is the order of the
factors.
If we expand both traces using (9.25), naturality of $\gamma_f$
lets us move the map $\gamma_g(K):g^{*}K(e)[2e]\to g^!K$
past the map $\gamma_f$ of the first trace. The composite then consists of
the two maps $\gamma_f$ and $\gamma_g$, which together are $\gamma_{g\circ f}(K)$ by
Proposition [proposition-compatibility-purity-composition], followed by

$$
Rg_!Rf_!f^!g^!K
\xrightarrow{\ Rg_!(\varepsilon_{f}(g^!K))\ }
Rg_!g^!K
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_{g}(K)\ }K.
$$

This is the counit of the composite adjunction
$R(g\circ f)_!\dashv(g\circ f)^!$, so the composite is the map $\gamma_{g\circ f}(K)$
followed by its counit, that is,
$\operatorname{Tr}_{g\circ f}(K)$.
This clause is proved by the proof of Proposition [proposition-transitivity-trace-map], with the hypotheses and choices shared there.

A twist to weight zero puts all local eigenvalues on the unit circle,
where inversion is complex conjugation. Adding the dual therefore makes
each multiset of eigenvalues stable under conjugation.

To find the twist, choose a closed point $x$, of degree $d$, at which the stalk is
nonzero, and a Frobenius eigenvalue $\alpha$ at $x$.  Let $b\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$
be a $d$th root of $\alpha^{-1}$.  By purity,
$|\iota(b)|=|\iota(\alpha)|^{-1/d}=q^{-w/2}$, and
Proposition [proposition-weights-under-usual-operations] shows that $\mathcal F^0$
is pure of weight zero.

Its local eigenvalues $\beta_j$ therefore have absolute value one after applying
$\iota$. The local eigenvalues of its dual are the $\beta_j^{-1}$, and
$\iota(\beta_j^{-1})=\overline{\iota(\beta_j)}$. So the union of the
two multisets is stable under complex conjugation, and
$\mathcal E$ is real and pure. In the same way, at a point $x$ over $k_n$ the
eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Frob}_{x,n}$ on $(\mathcal F^0)^\vee$ become,
after $\iota$, the complex conjugates of those on $\mathcal F^0$. Hence
$\iota$ of the trace of $(\mathcal F^0)^\vee$ is the complex conjugate of
$\iota$ of the trace of $\mathcal F^0$, and the trace of $\mathcal E$ is twice
its real part.

The dual has reciprocal eigenvalues, whose images are $\overline{\iota(\beta_j)}$. The union of these two multisets, the eigenvalue multiset of $\mathcal E$, is stable under conjugation. This is the asserted reality condition.

The inclusion into the first summand and projection onto it are morphisms of Weil sheaves and compose to the identity of $\mathcal F^0$, supplying the required direct summand.

K-injective resolutions of arbitrary complexes exist in the
Grothendieck category of $\mathcal R$-modules [Stacks, [079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P)], which
defines both functors. Both are right adjoints on derived categories:
$R\Gamma(U,-)$ is right adjoint to the functor sending a complex of
abelian groups $M$ to $\mathcal R[h_U]\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}M$,
where $\mathcal R[h_U]$ is the free $\mathcal R$-module on $h_U$, and
$Rf_*$ is right adjoint to the derived pullback of modules. Right
adjoints preserve products. Since (2.1) is built
from products and a cone, an exact functor preserving products also
preserves derived inverse limits [Stacks, [0940](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0940)].

The category of sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules is Grothendieck. Arbitrary complexes therefore admit K-injective resolutions by [Stacks, [079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P)]. Applying sections on $U$, respectively direct image along $f$, to these resolutions defines the two indicated derived functors on the unbounded derived categories.

*Source:* the proof of Proposition [proposition-unbounded-functors-products–1].

The functor $R\Gamma(U,-)$ is right adjoint to $M\mapsto\mathcal R[h_U]\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}M$, and $Rf_*$ is right adjoint to derived pullback. Hence both preserve products. They are exact functors of triangulated categories, and the cone formula (2.1) constructs the derived inverse limit from products and a cone. They therefore preserve that construction as well; see [Stacks, [0940](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0940)].
