objects.body:
Let $T$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq V\subseteq T$ be quasi-compact opens
with $U$ dense in $T$, and let $p:Y\to T$ be separated and of finite
type. Suppose that $f:U\to Y$ is a section of $p$ over $U$ and that
its image is closed in $p^{-1}(V)$. There are a $V$-admissible blow-up
$\pi:T'\to T$, an open $W\subseteq T'$ containing $\pi^{-1}(U)$,
and a map $g:W\to Y$ such that

$$
p\circ g=\pi|_W,\qquad
g|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}=f\circ\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(U)},
$$

and the graph of $g$ is closed in $Y\times_TT'$.

Let $T$ and $Y$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq V\subseteq T$ be quasi-compact
opens with $U$ dense in $T$, and let $p:Y\to T$ be separated,
quasi-compact and locally of finite type.
Suppose that $f:U\to Y$ is a section of $p$ over $U$ and that
its image is closed in $p^{-1}(V)$. There are a $V$-admissible blow-up
$\pi:T'\to T$, an open $W\subseteq T'$ containing $\pi^{-1}(U)$,
and a map $g:W\to Y$ such that

$$
p\circ g=\pi|_W,\qquad
g|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}=f\circ\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(U)},
$$

and the graph of $g$ is closed in $Y\times_TT'$.

Here quasi-compactness and local finite type of $p$ mean that $p$ is
of finite type. The explicit qcqs hypothesis on $Y$ follows from $T$
being qcqs and $p$ being separated and of finite type.

Let $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, $E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be separated
of finite type. Then $f^!$ maps $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$,
and this restriction is right adjoint to
$Rf_!:D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)\to D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y,\Lambda)$.
For $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$, one has $f^!_{\mathcal O_E}K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$.
For $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},E)$, one has $f^!_{E}K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},E)$.

For $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, one has $f^!_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$.

Let $(B,J)$ be a henselian pair, let $Y$ be proper over $B$, and put
$Y_0=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$. Then
restriction is an equivalence between the categories of finite étale
schemes over $Y$ and over $Y_0$,

$$
\textit{F\'Et}_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\textit{F\'Et}_{Y_0}.
$$

Consequently, for a finite abelian group $M$,

$$
H^1(Y,\underline M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(Y_0,\underline M).
\tag{4.8}
$$

attrs.title: Finite étale covers over a proper henselian pair

objects.body:
*Lifting finite étale covers over a proper henselian pair.*
Let $(B,J)$ be a henselian pair, let $Y$ be proper over $B$, and let
$i:Y_0\to Y$ be the closed fibre
$Y_0=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$.
Base change along $i$ is an equivalence between the categories of finite
étale schemes over $Y$ and over $Y_0$,

$$
\textit{F\'Et}_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}
\textit{F\'Et}_{Y_0}.
$$

This is [Stacks, [0GS2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GS2)], proved by algebraization, approximation, and
descent of finite presentation.

Let $(B,J)$ be a henselian pair, let $Y$ be proper over $B$, and let
$i:Y_0\to Y$ be the closed fibre over $B/J$. For every finite abelian
group $M$, restriction on étale cohomology is a bijection

$$
H^1(Y,\underline M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(Y_0,\underline M).
\tag{4.8}
$$

Here the target of the restriction map is first
$H^1(Y_0,i^*\underline M)$, which we identify with
$H^1(Y_0,\underline M)$ using the canonical isomorphism
$i^*\underline M\simeq\underline M$.

Indeed, these groups classify $M$-torsors, and the equivalence of
clause [theorem-finite-etale-covers-proper-henselian--2] transports finite étale covers, their group
actions, and the equations expressing simple transitivity.

Let $(B,J)$ be a henselian pair and let $G$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on
$\operatorname{Spec}(B)_{\acute{e}t}$. Then restriction induces isomorphisms

$$
H^q(\operatorname{Spec}B,G)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
H^q(\operatorname{Spec}(B/J),G|_{\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)})
\qquad(q\geq0).
$$

attrs.title: Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change

objects.body:
*Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change.*
If $(B,J)$ is a henselian pair and $G$ is a torsion abelian sheaf on
$\operatorname{Spec}(B)_{\acute{e}t}$, restriction induces

$$
H^q(\operatorname{Spec}B,G)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
H^q(\operatorname{Spec}(B/J),G|)
\qquad(q\geq0).
$$

This is [Stacks, [09ZI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZI)], and its proof is an effacement argument on affines.

Let $S$ be integral, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of
$S$-schemes. For a constructible
$\Fell$-sheaf $F$ on $X_{\acute{e}t}$, there is a nonempty open
$S_0\subset S$ such that

$$
Rj_{S_0,*}(F|_{X_{S_0}})\in\Dbc(Y_{S_0},\Fell),
\tag{6.19}
$$

and such that for every $k$-scheme $T\to S_0$ of finite type, with base change
$j_T:X_T\hookrightarrow Y_T$ and projections $g_X:X_T\to X_{S_0}$ and
$g_Y:Y_T\to Y_{S_0}$, the base change map

$$
\beta_T:g_Y^*Rj_{S_0,*}(F|_{X_{S_0}})
\longrightarrow Rj_{T,*}g_X^*(F|_{X_{S_0}})
\tag{6.20}
$$

is an isomorphism.

attrs.title: Generic constructibility and base change for $Rj_*$

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be integral and of finite type over $k$, and
let $Y\to S$ be of finite type. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring
such that some positive integer annihilating $\Lambda$ is invertible on
$S$, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion. We work on the
étale site, and write $\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$ for bounded complexes of étale
$\Lambda$-sheaves with constructible cohomology.

For a constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf $F$ on $X_{\acute{e}t}$, there is a
nonempty open $S_0\subset S$ such that for every noetherian scheme $T$
and every morphism $t:T\to S$ whose image lies in $S_0$, with base change
$j_T:X_T\hookrightarrow Y_T$ and projection $g_X:X_T\to X$, one has

$$
Rj_{T,*}g_X^*F\in\Dbc(Y_T,\Lambda).
$$

In particular, taking $T=S_0$ gives

$$
Rj_{S_0,*}(F|_{X_{S_0}})\in\Dbc(Y_{S_0},\Lambda).
\tag{6.19}
$$

attrs.title: Generic constructibility and base change for $Rj_*$ (1)

objects.body:
With the data of clause [theorem-generic-constructibility-base-change-rj--1], the same nonempty open $S_0$
can be chosen so that, for every noetherian scheme $T$ and every morphism
$t:T\to S$ whose image lies in $S_0$, the base change map

$$
g_Y^*Rj_*F\longrightarrow Rj_{T,*}g_X^*F
$$

is an isomorphism. Here $g_X:X_T\to X$ and $g_Y:Y_T\to Y$ are the
projections. Thus bounded constructibility and base change hold on one
open, uniformly for all such $T$; no finite type hypothesis on $T$ is
needed.

Equivalently, writing $F_0=F|_{X_{S_0}}$ and
$g_{X,0}:X_T\to X_{S_0}$, $g_{Y,0}:Y_T\to Y_{S_0}$ for the projections,
the map

$$
g_{Y,0}^*Rj_{S_0,*}F_0\longrightarrow Rj_{T,*}g_{X,0}^*F_0
\tag{6.20}
$$

is an isomorphism for every morphism $T\to S_0$ with $T$ noetherian.

Let $X_0$ be separated and of finite type over $\mathbf F_q$, put
$X=X_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and suppose
that $\ell\nmid q$. Let

$$
\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\},
\qquad K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda),
$$

with a Weil structure as in Definition [definition-weil-structure].
Here $A$ is any finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring, and for
integral and rational coefficients, $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)=\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.
Let $\operatorname{Frob}_{X,K}$
be the geometric Frobenius on $R\Gamma_c(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},K)$, and let
$\operatorname{Frob}_{y,m}$ be the Frobenius acting on the stalk $K_{\bar y}$ at
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$. Then for every $m\geq1$ we have, in $\Lambda$,

$$
\operatorname{tr}_{\Lambda}
\bigl(\operatorname{Frob}_{X,K}^m\mid R\Gamma_c(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},K)\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\operatorname{tr}_{\Lambda}
\bigl(\operatorname{Frob}_{y,m}\mid K_{\bar y}\bigr).
\tag{12.3}
$$

The complexes inside the traces are perfect over $\Lambda$, and the
formula is compatible with the change-of-coefficients maps of
Proposition [proposition-six-operations-change-coefficients]. For $\Lambda=\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, it reads

$$
\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl(\operatorname{Frob}_{X,K}^m\mid H_c^i(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},K)\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\sum_j(-1)^j
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\operatorname{Frob}_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{\bar y})\bigr),
\tag{12.4}
$$

where all sums over degrees are finite.
The complex $R\Gamma_c(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},K)$ inside the trace is perfect over $\Lambda$.
Each stalk $K_{\bar y}$ inside the local trace is perfect over $\Lambda$.
The trace formula is compatible with the coefficient comparisons of Proposition [proposition-six-operations-change-coefficients].

For $\Lambda=\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, it reads

$$
\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl(\operatorname{Frob}_{X,K}^m\mid H_c^i(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},K)\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\sum_j(-1)^j
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\operatorname{Frob}_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{\bar y})\bigr),
\tag{12.4}
$$

where all sums over degrees are finite.

The functor $\operatorname{Hilb}^{d}_{C/k}$ is represented by a smooth proper geometrically
integral $k$-scheme of dimension $d$, with $\operatorname{Hilb}^{0}_{C/k}=\operatorname{Spec}k$.
Its $T$-points are precisely the relative effective Cartier divisors
that are finite locally free of degree $d$. It has a universal
divisor $D_d\subset C\times_k\operatorname{Hilb}^{d}_{C/k}$ and an associated invertible sheaf
$\mathcal O(D_d)$.

attrs.title: Hilbert schemes of points on a smooth curve

objects.body:
Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral
curve over $k$, and let $d\geq0$. The functor
$\operatorname{Hilb}^{d}_{C/k}$ is represented by a smooth proper
geometrically integral $k$-scheme $H_d$ of dimension $d$, and
$H_0\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$.

For every $k$-scheme $T$, its $T$-points are the relative effective
Cartier divisors $D\subset C_T$ that are finite locally free of degree
$d$ over $T$. The identity of $H_d$ corresponds to a universal relative
effective Cartier divisor $D_d\subset C\times_k H_d$. If
$h:T\to H_d$ classifies $D_h$, then

$$
D_h=(1_C\times h)^*D_d,\qquad
\mathcal O(D_h)\simeq(1_C\times h)^*\mathcal O(D_d).
$$

Here $\mathcal O(D_d)$ is the dual of the invertible ideal of $D_d$.

Let $k$ be separably closed and let $C/k$ be a smooth proper
connected curve of genus $g$. The fppf Picard functor is represented
by a smooth separated group scheme, locally of finite type over $k$,
with a decomposition

$$
\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}
=\coprod_{d\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}.
$$

Each component is a smooth proper geometrically connected variety of
dimension $g$, parametrizing invertible sheaves of degree $d$.
The identity component
$J(C)=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is an abelian variety, and

$$
J(C)(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C),
\qquad T_0J(C)=H^1(C,\mathcal O_C).
$$

The formation of this representing scheme, its degree components
and $J(C)$ commutes with extension of the ground field.

attrs.title: The Picard scheme and the Jacobian over a separably closed field

objects.body:
Let $k$ be separably closed and let $C/k$ be a smooth proper
geometrically integral curve of genus $g$. The fppf Picard functor
is represented by a group scheme $\mathbf{Pic}_{C/k}$ whose group law
is induced by tensor product of invertible sheaves. Every representing
scheme is smooth of dimension $g$, in particular locally of finite type
over $k$, and the group scheme $\mathbf{Pic}_{C/k}$ is separated.

The degree $\delta:\mathbf{Pic}_{C/k}\to\mathbf Z$ of the universal
Picard class is locally constant. Its fibres give a decomposition

$$
\mathbf{Pic}_{C/k}=\coprod_{d\in\mathbf Z}\mathbf{Pic}^d_{C/k}
$$

into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes. Here
$\mathbf{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ represents $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, the fppf
sheafification of the subfunctor of invertible sheaves whose degree on
every fibre is $d$. The representations are compatible with the
inclusions $\mathbf{Pic}^d_{C/k}\hookrightarrow\mathbf{Pic}_{C/k}$: a
class of fibrewise degree $d$ determines the same point of
$\mathbf{Pic}_{C/k}$ through either representation.

Let $k$ and $C$ be as in
[theorem-picard-scheme-jacobian-over-separably--1]. For every
$d\in\mathbf Z$, any $k$-scheme representing
$\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ is smooth of dimension $g$, proper and
geometrically integral over $k$. In particular, each degree component
is a smooth proper geometrically connected variety of dimension $g$.

Let $k$ and $C$ be as in
[theorem-picard-scheme-jacobian-over-separably--1]. The degree-zero
functor $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is represented by a commutative
group scheme $J(C)$, proper, smooth of dimension $g$ and geometrically
integral over $k$. Its group law corresponds to tensor product of
invertible sheaves. Thus $J(C)$ is an abelian variety.

Put $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=\ker(\deg:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\mathbf Z)$.
There is a group isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)\simeq J(C)(k)
$$

sending an invertible sheaf of degree zero to the point classifying
its image in $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}(k)$.

attrs.title: The Picard scheme and the Jacobian over a separably closed field (4)

objects.body:
For a morphism $X\to S$ and a base change $S'\to S$, put
$X'=X\times_S S'$. Restricting $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ to schemes
over $S'$ gives a functor naturally isomorphic to
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X'/S'}$.

Let $k$ be any field, let $C/k$ be proper and locally of finite
presentation, and let $K/k$ be a field extension. For every
$d\in\mathbf Z$, the same identification restricts to the degree
parts:

$$
\left.\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}\right|_{K\text{-schemes}}
\simeq\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C_K/K}.
$$

Consequently, whenever these functors are represented, their
representing schemes commute with extension of the ground field.
This applies to the Picard scheme and its degree components in
[theorem-picard-scheme-jacobian-over-separably--1], and, for $d=0$,
to the Jacobian in [theorem-picard-scheme-jacobian-over-separably--3].

Let $X/k$ be smooth, separated of pure dimension $d$, with
$k$ algebraically closed. For every admissible $\Lambda$ and
$K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$, Theorem [theorem-smooth-purity-all-admissible-coefficients] gives isomorphisms

$$
\omega_X\simeq\Lambda_X(d)[2d],\qquad
\mathbb D_XK\simeq
\cHom_X(K,\Lambda_X)(d)[2d].
$$

Put $K^\vee=\cHom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$. If $K$ is locally perfect over
$\Lambda_X$, then so is $K^\vee$, and it is the ordinary dual. Let $\operatorname{Tr}_X$ be the map induced on $R\Gamma_c$ by
the trace map of $a_X$ (Definition [definition-trace-map]). The
pairing

$$
\begin{split}
\beta_K:\quad
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}
R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]
&\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d))[2d]\\
&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}_X}\Lambda
\end{split}
\tag{10.7}
$$

is perfect, and its adjoint is the canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]
\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\!\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda).
\tag{10.8}
$$

If $X$ is proper, $R\Gamma_c$ may be replaced by
$R\Gamma$. For a map $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ of admissible coefficient
rings, the change-of-coefficients isomorphisms of
Proposition [proposition-six-operations-change-coefficients] for
$R\Gamma_c$, $R\Gamma$ and $\cHom$ carry
$\beta_K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_\Lambda\Lambda'$ to $\beta_{K_{\Lambda'}}$,
where $K_{\Lambda'}=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_\Lambda\Lambda'$.

Let $X/k$ be smooth, separated of pure dimension $d$, with
$k$ algebraically closed. For every admissible $\Lambda$ and
$K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$, Theorem [theorem-smooth-purity-all-admissible-coefficients] gives isomorphisms

$$
\omega_X\simeq\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

$$
\mathbb D_XK\simeq\cHom_X(K,\Lambda_X)(d)[2d].
$$
Put $K^\vee=\cHom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$.

If $K$ is locally perfect over
$\Lambda_X$, then so is $K^\vee$,
and it is the ordinary dual.

Let $\operatorname{Tr}_X$ be the map induced on $R\Gamma_c$ by
the trace map of $a_X$ (Definition [definition-trace-map]). The
pairing

$$
\begin{split}
\beta_K:\quad
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}
R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]
&\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X(d))[2d]\\
&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}_X}\Lambda
\end{split}
\tag{10.7}
$$

is perfect,

and its adjoint is the canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]
\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\!\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda).
\tag{10.8}
$$

If $X$ is proper, $R\Gamma_c$ may be replaced by
$R\Gamma$.

For a map $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ of admissible coefficient
rings, the change-of-coefficients isomorphisms of
Proposition [proposition-six-operations-change-coefficients] for
$R\Gamma_c$, $R\Gamma$ and $\cHom$ carry
$\beta_K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_\Lambda\Lambda'$ to $\beta_{K_{\Lambda'}}$,
where $K_{\Lambda'}=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_\Lambda\Lambda'$.

Let $X_0/\mathbf F_q$ be smooth and separated of pure dimension
$d$, let $X=X_0\times\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let
$(K,\phi_K)$ be a Weil complex on $X$ (Definition [definition-weil-structure])
with $K$ locally perfect.
Equip the dual with the contragredient Weil structure

$$
\operatorname{Fr}_X^*K^\vee
\simeq(\operatorname{Fr}_X^*K)^\vee
\xrightarrow{\ (\phi_K^{-1})^\vee\ }K^\vee.
$$

For every admissible $\Lambda$ the Poincaré pairing $\beta_K$ of (10.7)
is a morphism of Weil complexes. Thus, with $F$ the Frobenius operators
defined above, the pairing
$H^i_c(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\to\Lambda$ satisfies
$\langle Fx,Fy\rangle=\langle x,y\rangle$, and the pairing
$H^i_c(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\to\Lambda(-d)$ satisfies

$$
\langle Fx,Fy\rangle=q^d\langle x,y\rangle.
$$

If $\Lambda$ is a field, then $F$ is invertible on $H^i_c(X,K)$, and
with respect to the second pairing $F$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)$ is $q^d$
times the inverse transpose of $F$ on $H^i_c(X,K)$. Hence the two
spaces have the same dimension $b$, the eigenvalues of $F$ on
$H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)$ are the $q^d/\alpha$, with multiplicities, where
$\alpha$ ranges over the eigenvalues on $H^i_c(X,K)$, and
$\det(F\mid H^i_c(X,K))\det(F\mid H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee))=q^{db}$.

Equip $K^\vee$ with the Weil structure

$$
\operatorname{Fr}_X^*K^\vee\simeq(\operatorname{Fr}_X^*K)^\vee
\xrightarrow{(\phi_K^{-1})^\vee}K^\vee.
$$
For every admissible $\Lambda$, the pairing $\beta_K$ of (10.7) is a morphism of Weil complexes.
The pairing between $H_c^i(X,K)$ and $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))$, with values in $\Lambda$, satisfies $\langle Fx,Fy\rangle=\langle x,y\rangle$.
The pairing between $H_c^i(X,K)$ and $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)$, with values in $\Lambda(-d)$, satisfies $\langle Fx,Fy\rangle=q^d\langle x,y\rangle$.
If $\Lambda$ is a field, then $F$ is invertible on $H_c^i(X,K)$.
If $\Lambda$ is a field, then with respect to the untwisted pairing, $F$ on $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)$ is $q^d$ times the inverse transpose of $F$ on $H_c^i(X,K)$.
Over a coefficient field the two spaces in the preceding clause have the same dimension, denoted by $b$.
Over a coefficient field the eigenvalues on $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)$ are $q^d/\alpha$, with multiplicities, where $\alpha$ runs over the eigenvalues on $H_c^i(X,K)$.
Over a coefficient field, $\det(F\mid H_c^i(X,K))\det(F\mid H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee))=q^{db}$.

*Shared context.* Let $X_0/\mathbf F_q$ be smooth and separated of pure dimension $d$, put $X=X_0\times\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let $(K,\phi_K)$ be a Weil complex with $K$ locally perfect. All pairings and Frobenius operators are those of the reference.

Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper
morphism of schemes, and let $g:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. Set
$X'=X\times_YY'$, with projections $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$.
Let $K\in D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$ have torsion
cohomology sheaves (as abelian sheaves). Then the base change map
(4.5) of Definition [definition-pro-etale-base-change-map]

$$
g^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^*K
$$

is an isomorphism in $D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(Y'_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$.

Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper
morphism of schemes, and let $g:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. Set
$X'=X\times_YY'$, with projections $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$.
Let $K\in D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$ have torsion
cohomology sheaves (as abelian sheaves). Then the base change map
(4.5) of Definition [definition-pro-etale-base-change-map]

$$

Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:C\to C'$ be proper, and let
$c'=(c'_1,c'_2):C'\to Y\times Y$ satisfy $c'_ig=fc_i$. Set $K'=Rf_*K$, and
let $u'$ be the pushforward of $u$ to $(Y,K')$ of
Definition [definition-pushforward-correspondence]. With
the induced proper map $h:\Fix(c)\to \Fix(c')$ one has

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{c'}(u')=h_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u).
$$

If $X$ and $C$ are proper over $k$, this gives

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma(X,K))
=\int_{\Fix(c)}\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)
=\sum_B\operatorname{LT}_B(u),
$$

for any finite open-and-closed decomposition $\Fix(c)=\coprod B$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:C\to C'$ be proper, and let
$c'=(c'_1,c'_2):C'\to Y\times Y$ satisfy $c'_ig=fc_i$. Set $K'=Rf_*K$, and
let $u'$ be the pushforward of $u$ to $(Y,K')$ of
Definition [definition-pushforward-correspondence]. With
the induced proper map $h:\Fix(c)\to \Fix(c')$ one has

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{c'}(u')=h_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u).
$$

If $X$ and $C$ are proper over $k$, this gives

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma(X,K))=\int_{\Fix(c)}\operatorname{Tr}_c(u).
$$

$$
\int_{\Fix(c)}\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\sum_B\operatorname{LT}_B(u).
$$

for any finite open-and-closed decomposition $\Fix(c)=\coprod B$.

attrs.title: Pure lisse sheaves over relative affine curves (1)

objects.body:
Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be smooth proper of pure relative dimension $d$,
and let $F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$w$. For every $i$, the canonical identification

$$
R^if_{0!}F=R^if_{0*}F
$$

is Weil-equivariant, and this constructible sheaf is punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w+i$. In particular, it is mixed of the
single weight $w+i$.

objects.body:
On a smooth geometrically connected curve over $\mathbf F_q$, every
irreducible constituent of an $\iota$-real lisse Weil sheaf is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight equal to its determinant weight.
In particular, every $\iota$-real lisse Weil sheaf on the curve is mixed.

attrs.title: Purity of real sheaves on curves

objects.body:
Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected curve over $\mathbf F_q$,
and let $\mathcal G$ be an $\iota$-real lisse Weil sheaf on $C_0$.
Suppose that $\mathcal G_1\subseteq\mathcal G_2\subseteq\mathcal G$
are lisse Weil subsheaves and that
$\mathcal V=\mathcal G_2/\mathcal G_1$ is irreducible lisse.
Then $\mathcal V$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$\gamma=\operatorname{dw}_\iota(\mathcal V)$. At every closed point $x$,

$$
\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal V)\gamma
=\frac{2\log\bigl|\iota\det(\operatorname{Frob}_x\mid\mathcal V_{\bar x})\bigr|}{\log q_x}.
$$

Equivalently, if $\rho$ is an $\iota$-real lisse representation of
$W(C_0)$ and $\sigma$ is an irreducible constituent of $\rho$ of
determinant weight $\gamma$, then $\sigma$ is punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $\gamma$.

attrs.title: Purity of real sheaves on curves (1)

objects.body:
Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected curve over $\mathbf F_q$.
Every $\iota$-real lisse Weil sheaf on $C_0$ is $\iota$-mixed.

attrs.title: Purity of real sheaves on curves (2)

objects.body:
Let $U_0/k_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected curve, and let
$\chi:W(U_0)\to E^\times$ be the character of a rank-one lisse Weil
sheaf.  Then $\chi(\pi_1(U))$ is finite.

attrs.title: Rank-one sheaves have finite geometric monodromy

objects.body:
Let $U_0/k_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected curve over a finite
field, and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ be prime. Let $W(U_0)$ be
its Weil group, with geometric subgroup $\ker(\deg)=\pi_1(U)$ as in
[sec-Weil-sheaves-and-weights].
If $\chi:W(U_0)\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$ is a character whose
restriction to $\pi_1(U)$ is continuous, then there is an integer $N>0$
such that

$$
\chi(g)^N=1\qquad(g\in\pi_1(U)).
$$

In particular, $\chi(\pi_1(U))$ is finite.

attrs.title: A uniform exponent for the geometric character

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes of finite type over $k$.

1. (Proper base change) If $f$ is proper, then for every morphism of schemes
   $g:S'\to S$, not necessarily of finite type over $k$, and every $K\in D(X_{\acute{e}t},A)$, the base change map
   $g^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g'^*K$ is an isomorphism, where $f':X'\to S'$ and
   $g':X'\to X$ are the projections of $X'=X\times_SS'$. In particular, the
   geometric stalks of $Rf_*K$ are the cohomology of the geometric fibres.
2. (Finiteness) If $f$ is separated, then $Rf_!$ maps $\Dbc(X,A)$ into
   $\Dbc(S,A)$.
3. (Cohomological dimension) The functors $Rf_*$ and, if $f$ is
   separated, $Rf_!$ have finite cohomological amplitude on torsion
   sheaves. In particular $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(f)<\infty$ in the sense of
   Definition [definition-cohomological-dimension].

*Proper base change*: let $p:X\to S$ be proper, let $g:S'\to S$ be
a morphism, and let $p':X'\to S'$, $g':X'\to X$ be the projections of
$X'=X\times_SS'$. For $K\in D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$, the
base change map $g^*Rp_*K\to Rp'_*g'^*K$ is
an isomorphism. On the étale site this is
Theorem [theorem-proper-base-change-classical-pro] for bounded below torsion complexes
and [Stacks, [0F0C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0C)] for unbounded complexes with finite coefficients, and
by comparison it holds on the pro-étale site.

In particular, the
geometric stalk of $Rp_*K$ is the pro-étale cohomology of the fibre.

*Finiteness*: for $f$ separated of finite type,
[Stacks, [0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0)] says, after comparison with the étale site, that $Rf_!$ maps
$\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dbc(S,\Lambda)$.

For a morphism $f:X\to S$ of finite-type $k$-schemes, $Rf_*$ has finite cohomological amplitude on classical torsion sheaves, by the étale bound [Stacks, [0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10)] and comparison.

Under the applicability hypotheses for $Rf_!$, the same bound holds for $Rf_!:D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\Lambda)\to D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(S_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\Lambda)$ on classical torsion coefficient sheaves.
Consequently $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(f)<\infty$ in the sense of Definition [definition-cohomological-dimension].
*Shared context.* The coefficients, classical complexes and finite-type hypotheses are exactly those in the reference's recalled étale results.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $C$ we have

$$
\chi(C,\mathcal L)=\deg\mathcal L+1-g,
\qquad
H^1(C,\mathcal L)^\vee
\simeq H^0(C,\omega_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}),
\qquad \deg\omega_{C/k}=2g-2,
\qquad \dim_kH^0(C,\omega_{C/k})=g.
$$

In particular, if
$\deg\mathcal L>2g-2$, then

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal L)=0,
\qquad h^0(C,\mathcal L)=\deg\mathcal L+1-g.
$$

Let $C$ be a smooth proper curve over a field $k$ such that
$k\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is an isomorphism, and put
$g=h^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$. For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $C$,
the cohomology of $\mathcal L$ is finite-dimensional and vanishes above
degree one, and the cohomological degree
$\chi(C,\mathcal L)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$ agrees with the divisor degree
$\deg\mathcal L$. Since $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=1-g$, this gives

$$
\chi(C,\mathcal L)=\deg\mathcal L+1-g.
$$

Let $C$ be a smooth proper curve over a field $k$, and put
$\omega_{C/k}=\Omega^1_{C/k}$. For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $C$
there is a $k$-linear isomorphism

$$
H^1(C,\mathcal L)^\vee
\simeq H^0(C,\omega_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}).
$$

No assumption on $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is needed.

Let $C$ be a smooth proper curve over a field $k$ such that
$k\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is an isomorphism, and put
$g=h^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$. Then

$$
\deg\omega_{C/k}=2g-2.
$$

Let $C$ be a smooth proper curve over a field $k$ such that
$k\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is an isomorphism, and put
$g=h^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$. If $\mathcal L$ is invertible and
$2g-1\leq\deg\mathcal L$, then

$$
h^1(C,\mathcal L)=0.
$$

Since $H^1(C,\mathcal L)$ is finite-dimensional, this is equivalent to
$H^1(C,\mathcal L)=0$. The degree is an integer, so the hypothesis is
equivalent to $\deg\mathcal L>2g-2$.

Let $C$ be a smooth proper curve over a field $k$ such that
$k\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is an isomorphism, and put
$g=h^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$. If $\mathcal L$ is invertible and
$2g-1\leq\deg\mathcal L$, then, as an equality of integers,

$$
h^0(C,\mathcal L)=\deg\mathcal L+1-g.
$$

For a smooth proper curve $C$ over any field $k$, one has

$$
\dim_kH^0(C,\omega_{C/k})=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)=g.
$$

In (8.1), assume that all schemes are of finite type over $k$
and that $g$ is smooth. For every admissible coefficient ring

$$
\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}
$$

and every $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$, the
base change map (4.5) is an isomorphism

$$
g^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^*K.
\tag{8.2}

attrs.title: Smooth base change for all admissible coefficients

objects.body:
For the finite-coefficient step we use the following more general
statement. In the cartesian square (8.1), let $g$ be
smooth and $f$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $A$ be a discrete
commutative ring killed by a positive integer $N$ whose image in
$\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is a unit. Suppose that
$K\in D(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},A)$ is of bounded constructible étale origin: there
are a $K_{\acute{e}t}\in\Dbc(X_{\acute{e}t},A)$ and an isomorphism
$\nu_X^*K_{\acute{e}t}\simeq K$. Then the map (4.5)

$$
g^*_{A}Rf_{*,A}K\longrightarrow Rf'_{*,A}g'^*_{A}K
\tag{8.2}
$$

is an isomorphism. No finite Tor amplitude or finite-type hypothesis over
$k$ is required in this statement. In particular, under the hypotheses of
the theorem, (8.2) is an isomorphism for every
$K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},A)$ when $A$ is a finite ring killed by a power of
$\ell$.

For $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal O_E)$, the map

$$
g^*_{\mathcal O_E}Rf_{*,\mathcal O_E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_{*,\mathcal O_E}g'^*_{\mathcal O_E}K
$$

is an isomorphism.

For $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},E)$, the map

$$
g^*_{E}Rf_{*,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_{*,E}g'^*_{E}K
$$

is an isomorphism.

For $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, the map

$$
g^*_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}Rf_{*,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_{*,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}g'^*_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}K
$$

is an isomorphism.

*Shared context.* Use the cartesian square (8.1). All its schemes are of finite type over $k$, and $g$ is smooth. The comparison is (4.5). Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, so $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Q_\ell$ occur when $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

attrs.title: Smooth base change for all admissible coefficients

objects.body:
In (8.1), suppose $g$ is smooth and $f$ is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $F$ be a classical torsion
abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$ which is the filtered union of its

objects.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d$. For every
admissible coefficient ring $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$,
with $A$ finite, there are isomorphisms, natural in $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y,\Lambda)$,

$$
\gamma_f(K):
f^{*}K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{!}K,
\tag{9.2}
$$

with the following properties.

1. If $f$ is the projection $p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$, then
   $\varepsilon_p(\Lambda_Y)\circ Rp_!\bigl(\gamma_p(\Lambda_Y)\bigr)$ is the
   trace map (9.1).
2. For $g:Y'\to Y$ as in
   Definition [definition-exceptional-base-change-map], with exceptional
   base change map $\beta:g'^*f^!K\to f'^!g^*K$, we have
   $\beta\circ g'^*\gamma_f(K)=\gamma_{f'}(g^*K)$, the sources being
   identified by $g'^*f^*\simeq f'^*g^*$.
3. For a smooth morphism $h:Y\to Z$ of pure relative dimension $e$ and
   $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Z,\Lambda)$, the map $\gamma_{h\circ f}(K)$ is the composite of
   $f^*(\gamma_h(K))(d)[2d]$ and $\gamma_f(h^!K)$, the sources being identified
   by $(h\circ f)^*\simeq f^*h^*$ and the targets by the composition
   isomorphism $f^!h^!\simeq(h\circ f)^!$ of
   Proposition [proposition-composition-open-restriction-compactifications-f](1).
4. For a coefficient map $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ of
   Proposition [proposition-six-operations-change-coefficients], the
   change-of-coefficients isomorphism $(f^!K)_{\Lambda'}\to f^!(K_{\Lambda'})$
   of that proposition carries $(\gamma_{f,\Lambda}(K))_{\Lambda'}$ to
   $\gamma_{f,\Lambda'}(K_{\Lambda'})$, the sources being identified by the
   change-of-coefficients isomorphism for $f^*$.

sheaf on $X\times Y\times Z$. If the restrictions of $\mathcal L$ to
$x\times Y\times Z$, $X\times y\times Z$ and $X\times Y\times z$ are
trivial, then $\mathcal L$ is trivial.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be proper geometrically integral $k$-schemes with points
$x\in X(k)$ and $y\in Y(k)$, let $Z$ be a connected $k$-scheme of finite
type with a point $z\in Z(k)$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible
sheaf on $X\times Y\times Z$. If the restrictions of $\mathcal L$ to
$x\times Y\times Z$, $X\times y\times Z$ and $X\times Y\times z$ are
trivial, then $\mathcal L$ is trivial.

Let $X_0$ be separated and of finite type over $\mathbf F_q$, let
$\Lambda\in\{\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, and let $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ carry a Weil
structure, with stalk Frobenius maps $\operatorname{Frob}_{y,m}$ as in
Theorem [theorem-grothendieck-lefschetz-trace-formula]. For each closed
point $x\in|X_0|$, let $\deg(x)=[\kappa(x):\mathbf F_q]$ be its degree,
choose one of the $\deg(x)$ points $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^{\deg(x)}})$ lying
over $x$, write $\bar x=\bar y$ for the corresponding geometric point,
and let $\operatorname{Frob}_x=\operatorname{Frob}_{y,\deg(x)}$ be its
action on $K_{\bar x}$. Another choice of $y$ replaces
$\operatorname{Frob}_x$ by a conjugate. Define

$$
L(X_0,K,T)
:=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}
\det\bigl(1-T^{\deg(x)}\operatorname{Frob}_x\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)^{-1}.
\tag{12.6}
$$

For every $n$, only finitely many factors differ from $1$ modulo $T^n$,
so the product converges $T$-adically in $1+T\Lambda[[T]]$, and

$$
L(X_0,K,T)
=\prod_i\det\bigl(1-T\operatorname{Frob}_{X,K}\mid H_c^i(X_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},K)\bigr)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
\tag{12.7}
$$

In particular, $L(X_0,K,T)$ is the expansion at zero of a rational
function in $\Lambda(T)$ with value $1$ at zero. If $X_0$ is proper, we
may replace $H_c^i$ by $H^i$.

Let $S$ be a scheme of finite type and of dimension at most $d$ over a
separably closed field $k'$, and let $A$ be a finite abelian group whose order
is invertible in $k'$. Write $\mathcal C_A$ for the sheaf
$V\mapsto C(V,A)$ on $S_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$. Then

$$
H^i(S_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal C_A)=0\qquad(i\notin[0,2d]).
$$

In particular $H^i(X,A_X)=0$ for $i\notin[0,2d]$; properness, smoothness and
connectedness of $X$ are not needed for this.
The specified trace $\operatorname{tr}_X:H^{2d}(X,A_X)\to A(-d)$ is an isomorphism.

Let $S$ and $k'$ be as in clause [theorem-trace-isomorphism-top-degree--2]. Let $A$ be a compact
topological abelian group with a decreasing sequence of open subgroups
$U_0\supset U_1\supset\cdots$ such that $\bigcap_nU_n=0$ and every quotient
$A/U_n$ has order invertible in $k'$. For the sheaf
$\mathcal C_A:V\mapsto C(V,A)$ on $S_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t}$,

$$
H^i(S_{\mathrm{pro}\acute{e}t},\mathcal C_A)=0\qquad(i\notin[0,2d]).
$$

This applies to $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $U_n=\pi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ when
$\ell$ is invertible in $k'$, and then $\mathcal C_A=\mathcal O_{E,S}$. In
particular $H^i(X,\mathcal O_{E,X})=0$ for $i\notin[0,2d]$.
The specified trace $\operatorname{tr}_X:H^{2d}(X,\mathcal O_{E,X})\to \mathcal O_E(-d)$ is an isomorphism.
$H^i(X,E_X)=0$ for $i\notin[0,2d]$.
The specified trace $\operatorname{tr}_X:H^{2d}(X,E_X)\to E(-d)$ is an isomorphism.

Let $S$ be a scheme of finite type and of dimension at most $d$ over a
separably closed field $k'$ in which $\ell$ is invertible. Then

$$
H^i(S,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,S})=0\qquad(i\notin[0,2d]).
$$

In particular $H^i(X,\QbarX)=0$ for $i\notin[0,2d]$; properness and
connectedness of $X$ are not needed for this.
The specified trace $\operatorname{tr}_X:H^{2d}(X,\QbarX)\to \overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-d)$ is an isomorphism.

*Shared context.* Let $X/k$ be smooth, proper and connected of pure dimension $d$, with $k$ algebraically closed. The trace in every clause is the twist by $(-d)$ of the map on $H^{2d}$ induced by Definition [definition-trace-map]; these are the original trace maps.

attrs.title: Weights and sums of squared traces (1)

objects.body:
Let $X_0/\mathbf F_q$ be smooth proper of pure dimension $d$, and let
$P_{i,\ell}$ be as above.

1. There are unique polynomials $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $P_i(0)=1$
   whose images in $\mathbf Q_\ell[T]$ are $P_{i,\ell}(T)$ for every prime
   $\ell\nmid q$, and
   $Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$.
2. The reciprocal roots of $P_i$ are algebraic integers, and each of them
   has absolute value $q^{i/2}$ under every complex embedding.
3. The degrees $b_i=\deg P_i=\dim_{\mathbf Q_\ell}H^i_\ell$ do not depend on $\ell$,
   and $b_i=b_{2d-i}$. If $X_0$ is geometrically connected, then
   $P_0=1-T$, $P_{2d}=1-q^dT$, and $b_0=b_{2d}=1$.
4. Put $\chi=\sum_i(-1)^ib_i$. Then $d\chi$ is even and there
   is $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ such that
   $$
   Z\!\left(X_0,\frac1{q^dT}\right)
   =\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
   \quad\hbox{in }\mathbf Q(T).
   $$

attrs.title: The Weil conjectures for smooth proper schemes

objects.body: There are polynomials $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $P_i(0)=1$ whose images in $\mathbf Q_\ell[T]$ are $P_{i,\ell}(T)$ for every prime $\ell\nmid q$.
If $X_0$ is geometrically connected, then $P_0=1-T$.
If $X_0$ is geometrically connected, then $P_{2d}=1-q^dT$.
If $X_0$ is geometrically connected, then $b_0=1$.
If $X_0$ is geometrically connected, then $b_{2d}=1$.
Define $\chi=\sum_i(-1)^ib_i$.
The integer $d\chi$ is even.

There is $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ such that

$$
Z\!\left(X_0,\frac1{q^dT}\right)=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
\quad\hbox{in }\mathbf Q(T).
$$
The family of polynomials satisfying the preceding normalization and comparison conditions is unique.
Every reciprocal root of $P_i$ is an algebraic integer.
Every reciprocal root of $P_i$ has absolute value $q^{i/2}$ under every complex embedding.
Define $b_i=\deg P_i$.

Let $K$ be a field and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space
with an automorphism $F$. Then

$$
\deg\det(1-TF\mid V)=\dim_KV.
$$

In particular, since Frobenius acts on $H^i_\ell$ by an automorphism,
$b_i=\deg P_i=\deg P_{i,\ell}=\dim_{\mathbf Q_\ell}H^i_\ell$ for every
prime $\ell\nmid q$.
The numbers $\dim_{\mathbf Q_\ell}H^i_\ell$ do not depend on $\ell$.
One has $b_i=b_{2d-i}$.

*Shared context.* Let $X_0/\mathbf F_q$ be smooth proper of pure dimension $d$, and let $P_{i,\ell}$ be as above. Throughout this block, $P_i$ denotes the same family specified in the first two clauses. The original items (1)–(4) are retained.
